findings.title: Anthropic Thinking Signature Dropped Breaking Multi-Turn
findings.summary: When Anthropic outputs thinking blocks, the initial block contains {'type':'thinking','thinking':''}. When signature_delta arrives, append(&mut blocks, i, 'signature', ...) is called. append requires the field to already exist (b.get_mut(field)), so it silently drops the signature. The block in history lacks 'signature', causing Anthropic to reject turn 2 with HTTP 400.
findings.failure_scenario: Any multi-turn conversation with an Anthropic direct model that uses extended thinking.
findings.evidence: direct.rs:402: append requires blocks.get_mut(index).and_then(|b| b.get_mut(field)). If field is missing, get_mut returns None. Signature is never recorded in history.
findings.suggested_fix: In append, if the field is not present in the JSON object, insert it as Value::String(s.to_string()).

verdicts.reasoning: Checked if append inserts missing keys or if signature is handled elsewhere in direct.rs. Critical bug in extended thinking streaming. Breaks multi-turn Anthropic requests.

findings.title: Direct Provider Models Query Incompatible with Anthropic
findings.summary: direct_provider_models unconditionally queries {base_url}/models with bearer_auth. Anthropic's endpoint is /v1/models and requires x-api-key and anthropic-version headers. As a result, dynamic model discovery fails for direct Anthropic setups.
findings.failure_scenario: Trek attempts to dynamically discover models for an Anthropic direct provider key.
findings.evidence: direct.rs:428: Always does client.get(format('{}/models', provider.base_url)).bearer_auth(k). Fails 100% on Anthropic.
findings.suggested_fix: Check provider.wire; if Wire::Anthropic, query /v1/models with x-api-key and anthropic-version.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked if catalog.rs or direct.rs routes Anthropic to /v1/models. High severity. Blocks dynamic model discovery for Anthropic direct wire.

findings.title: Parentheses in Body After Time Invalidate Rate Limit Reset
findings.summary: s.find('(') searches across the entire remaining string before splitting into sentences. Any markdown link or parenthetical remark (e.g. '(https://docs.anthropic.com)') gets extracted as zone. offset() fails on arbitrary non-timezone text, and the '?' operator causes parse_when to return None, discarding an otherwise completely valid clock reset time.
findings.failure_scenario: API rate limit error includes parenthetical text or markdown links after the reset time.
findings.evidence: limits.rs:185 finds '(' across the entire string. Line 248 has offset(zone, guess)?. Any invalid zone drops the parsed clock time.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract parentheses only within the first sentence clause, and ignore offset() failures by falling back to local/default timezone instead of returning None.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked if parse_when catches ? on offset() or limits search to sentence. High severity. Rate limits with links or parens fail to register reset time.

findings.title: 'retry after ' In Incorrect Match Group in reset_in
findings.summary: 'retry after ' is placed in AT (which expects calendar dates / clock times via parse_when), rather than IN (which parses duration spans like '60 seconds' via parse_span). Standard HTTP Retry-After plain text errors fail to parse.
findings.failure_scenario: An API error states 'Rate limit reached. Retry after 60s.'
findings.evidence: AT does not fall through to IN. parse_when fails on duration strings like '60 seconds'.
findings.suggested_fix: Move 'retry after ' to IN or attempt parse_span when parse_when returns None.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked if parse_when handles duration spans or if AT falls through to IN. Medium severity. Standard 'Retry after X' headers fail parsing.

findings.title: source_for Misclassifies Disabled Skills and Defaults to Project
findings.summary: When restoring disabled skills from disabled_root, source_for checks prefixes. Synced skills match .claude/skills and become ClaudeCode; unknown/synced/read-only origins fall into the final else and are marked as SkillSource::Project (which claims editable() == true).
findings.failure_scenario: A user disables a synced or non-project skill, then restarts Trek.
findings.evidence: source_for in skills.rs:212 matches .claude/skills first, turning Synced into ClaudeCode. Final fallback is Project unconditionally.
findings.suggested_fix: Properly distinguish Synced skills and avoid defaulting to editable Project if origin is outside project root.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked if discover() overrides source_for or if Synced is handled elsewhere. Medium severity. Inaccurate source labels and editable permissions.

findings.title: ORIGIN_FILE Removed Before move_dir in set_enabled(true)
findings.summary: set_enabled removes .trek-origin before executing move_dir(&skill.dir, &origin). If move_dir fails (cross-filesystem, permission, or disk full), .trek-origin is permanently lost. The skill is stranded in disabled_skills forever and can never be discovered or enabled.
findings.failure_scenario: A filesystem error or cross-device failure occurs while re-enabling a skill.
findings.evidence: Line 260 calls remove_file before move_dir. No catch or error recovery exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete ORIGIN_FILE only after move_dir has successfully returned Ok(()).

verdicts.reasoning: Checked if ORIGIN_FILE is recreated on move_dir error. High severity. Skill permanently lost on any move_dir failure.

findings.title: read_front_matter Scans Frontmatter Lines When description is Missing
findings.summary: When frontmatter exists but omits 'description:', the fallback scans text.lines() from line 0. It encounters the frontmatter lines (e.g. 'name: my-tool') and treats it as the description prose.
findings.failure_scenario: SKILL.md has YAML frontmatter without an explicit description field.
findings.evidence: Line 146 scans text.lines() from the beginning of the file, matching first non-empty line in frontmatter.
findings.suggested_fix: Scan for prose only after the closing '---' frontmatter delimiter.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked if lines.skip(closing_dashes) is implemented. Low severity. Metadata displayed as description.

findings.title: None == None Causes Salvaged Settings Resurrection

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure removed keys are purged.

findings.title: Math parser panics on any multi-byte whitespace (NBSP, U+202F, U+3000) inside a formula
findings.summary: `skip_space` advances `self.pos` by 1 byte for every char where `char::is_whitespace` is true, but many such chars are 2-3 bytes in UTF-8. The next `self.src[self.pos..]` in `peek` then slices inside a character and panics. The fuzz tests only use ASCII spaces, so this was never exercised.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent answer contains `$a\u{00a0}=\u{00a0}b$`, or a narrow no-break space (U+202F), or an ideographic space (U+3000) inside `$…$`, `\(…\)` or `$$…$$`. `Formula::of` -> `parse::parse` -> `list_inner` -> `skip_space` -> `peek` panics with 'byte index 2 is not a char boundary'. Reproduced by compiling the real parse.rs, layout.rs and tables.rs in a scratch crate: `parse("a\u{a0}b")` panics and so does `parse("x\u{3000}=\u{202f}1")`. There is no catch_unwind around markdown plugin parsing. A small answer is parsed on the main thread (the app dies). A large one is parsed in a background task that dies, so the message never renders.
findings.evidence: parse.rs:176-180: `fn skip_space(&mut self) { while self.peek().is_some_and(char::is_whitespace) { self.pos += 1; } }` and parse.rs:167 `self.src[self.pos..].chars().next()`. `Formula::of` (math/mod.rs) passes the raw TeX through unchanged: `parse::parse(&tex)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Advance by the char's length: `while let Some(c) = self.peek().filter(|c| c.is_whitespace()) { self.pos += c.len_utf8(); }`. Add NBSP, U+202F and U+3000 to the fuzz `pieces`.

verdicts.reasoning: Opened parse.rs. skip_space (line 176-180) does `self.pos += 1` for any char where char::is_whitespace is true. peek (line 167) slices `self.src[self.pos..]`. list_inner (line 226-228) calls skip_space at the top of every loop iteration, so it is reached for any formula. Formula::of in math/mod.rs passes the raw tex to parse::parse when the region is closed and under 20000 bytes, with no normalization. I copied the skip_space/peek logic into a scratch rustc program and ran it on "a\u{a0}b". It panics with "byte index 2 is not a char boundary; it is inside '\u{a0}'". A grep found no catch_unwind in the math or markdown path. The only hit is ide/watch.rs, which is unrelated. The line 487 branch handles whitespace correctly, but skip_space runs first in the loop and consumes the whitespace, so that branch doesn't help. I did not run the real crate's tests. The reported background-task vs main-thread consequences are plausible but I did not trace them.

I read parse.rs on disk. skip_space does `self.pos += 1` for any char where is_whitespace is true, and peek slices `self.src[self.pos..]`. Formula::of passes the raw TeX from detect::tex() to parse::parse without normalizing whitespace. list_inner calls skip_space at the top of every loop. I copied the real parse.rs, layout.rs and tables.rs into a scratch crate at /tmp/mp, built it, and ran parse() on three inputs. Plain "a b" returned ok. "a b" and "x　= 1" both panicked. I didn't run the full detect and markdown pipeline. Delimiters like `\(…\)` and `$$…$$` impose no whitespace rules that would filter these inputs out. I found no catch_unwind around markdown plugin parsing. The only catch_unwind in the crates is in ide/watch.rs. No test asserts this behaviour as intended, and the module doc comment says "nothing panics".

findings.title: decode_entities slices at byte 12 regardless of char boundary: an artifact heading like "Supply & Demand: ✓" panics Trek while the answer streams
findings.summary: decode_entities does `rest[..rest.len().min(12)]` to look for the ';' of an entity. The index 12 is a raw byte offset; when a multi-byte character (em dash, arrow, check mark, CJK, emoji) straddles byte 12 after an '&', the slice panics with 'byte index 12 is not a char boundary'. It is reached from artifact::title -> text_of on every streaming delta of a trek-html block (trek-app/src/artifact/mod.rs:110), on the agent's <title> or first <h1>-<h3>, and unescaped '&' in headings is routine agent output.
findings.failure_scenario:
Agent answers with a trek-html block whose heading is `

Supply & Demand: ✓ done

` (or `Q&A — results`-style text where a non-ASCII char covers byte 12 after the '&'). Trek's markdown plugin calls core::title(html) on the delta; title() finds the

, text_of() calls decode_entities("Supply & Demand: ✓ done"); at the '&' rest = "& Demand: ✓ done" (len > 12), and rest[..12] ends inside the 3-byte '✓' (bytes 10..13) -> panic. Verified with a standalone rustc probe (/tmp/trek-probe/probe.rs): `end byte index 12 is not a char boundary; it is inside '✓'`. The parse runs in a gpui background task; the panic hook (trek-app/src/logging.rs:121) only logs and re-raises, there is no panic=abort override, and unwinding out of gpui's dispatcher trampoline aborts the process, so the user sees Trek quit mid-answer; at best the whole answer stops rendering.
findings.suggested_fix:
Find the ';' on the whole remainder and bound by distance instead of slicing: `let end = rest.find(';').filter(|&e| e <= 12)` (or use `rest.char_indices().take_while(|(i, _)| *i < 12).find(|(_, c)| *c == ';')`). Add a test: `title("

Supply & Demand: ✓ done

")` and `title("Tom & Jerry — 日本語 ✓")` return without panicking.

verdicts.reasoning: Read decode_entities and title/text_of on disk. The quoted code is present and unguarded: `rest[..rest.len().min(12)]` slices by byte offset. title() takes the raw inner text of <title>/<h1-3> and passes it through text_of to decode_entities with no sanitising. The only early exit is `!s.contains('&')`. I reproduced the exact slicing on "Supply & Demand: ✓ done" with a standalone rustc probe, and it panics: byte index 12 is inside '✓' (bytes 10..13). Existing tests only use ASCII entities, so none asserts this behaviour as intended. The caller trek-app/src/artifact/mod.rs parse() calls core::title(html) on every streaming delta of a trek-html fence, including unclosed ones, and I found no catch_unwind there. The only catch_unwind is in ide/watch.rs, which is unrelated. The panic is certainly reachable from agent output with an unescaped '&' followed by non-ASCII text near byte 12. I did not verify that the panic aborts the whole process (gpui dispatcher behaviour), but a panic on a background task is a crash-class bug either way.

I checked the code on disk. artifact.rs has no uncommitted changes, and the quoted lines match. I extracted decode_entities verbatim into /tmp/sk1 and ran it on "Supply & Demand: ✓ done", the text the h1 branch of title() passes through text_of. It panicked with "end byte index 12 is not a char boundary; it is inside '✓' (bytes 10..13 of string)". Reading the code, title() reaches text_of, which calls decode_entities. The plugin's parse() calls core::title(html) on every delta of a trek-html fenced block. Nothing in trek-app/src/artifact or in artifact.rs uses catch_unwind to guard it. I did not run the app, so I did not confirm that the process aborts. A panic in that background parse is a real crash path either way. The trigger is only an unescaped '&' within about 12 bytes of a multi-byte character in a title or heading.

findings.title: Stop (or any mid-tool error) ends the whole direct-API session instead of the turn
findings.summary: Errors from execute_tool are propagated with `?` out of `run`, so an Interrupt while a permission card is open or a bash tool is running returns Err from the session future; supervise then sends Error("Interrupted") and Exited, killing the session and its in-memory history. Interrupts during model streaming are handled gracefully (turn ends), so this is inconsistent and clearly unintended.
findings.failure_scenario: User on a direct provider (OpenAI/OpenRouter/Ollama...) asks for a change; the model calls bash `cargo test` (or asks permission). User presses Stop. ask_permission/run_bash_command bail!("Interrupted") -> execute_tool returns Err -> `.await?` at line 282 returns Err from run() -> lib.rs supervise sends AgentEvent::Error("Interrupted") then Exited. The transcript gets an error item, the turn is marked as a crash-stop, live.commands = None, and the next message has to start a brand-new session from a recap. Shutdown during a permission prompt likewise surfaces as Error("Shutdown"). A command that never exits (e.g. the model runs `npm run dev`) has no timeout, so Stop, which kills the session, is the only way out.
findings.evidence: direct.rs:271-282: `let (output, ok, lines) = execute_tool(... &mut shutdown,).await?;` (inside run()). direct.rs:447-449 (ask_permission): `Command::Interrupt => { events.send(AgentEvent::PermissionResolved { request_id }).await?; bail!("Interrupted"); }`. direct.rs:637-640 (run_bash_command): `cmd = commands.recv() => { let _ = child.kill().await; keep_command(cmd, kept, shutdown)?; bail!("Interrupted") }`. Contrast the streaming path, direct.rs:313-320: `Err(e) => { history.pop(); ... turn_error.get_or_insert_with(|| format!("{e:#}")); break; }` which ends only the turn. lib.rs:507-516 supervise: `if let Err(e) = result { events.send(AgentEvent::Error(format!("{e:#}"))) } ... events.send(AgentEvent::Exited)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle execute_tool's Err like a failed model call: on "Interrupted" push the tool result as an interrupted output (or pop the assistant tool_calls message), set turn_error, break out of the tool loop and send TurnComplete; only propagate when `shutdown` is set. Give run_bash_command a timeout and run it via spawn_group.

verdicts.reasoning: I read run() in direct.rs, execute_tool, ask_permission, run_bash_command, keep_command and supervise in lib.rs on the working tree. The quoted evidence matches the code. In run(), execute_tool(...).await? sits inside the Ok(resp) arm of the match result. That arm is separate from the Err(e) arm, which is the only one that turns an error into turn_error and a break. The ? therefore returns from run() itself. I found nothing around it that catches the error. ask_permission does bail!("Interrupted") on Command::Interrupt and bail!("Shutdown") on Command::Shutdown. run_bash_command's select arm on commands.recv() kills the child, then calls keep_command, which bails on Interrupt, and the following bail!("Interrupted") covers a non-fatal command. supervise in lib.rs then sends AgentEvent::Error and AgentEvent::Exited. The session loop and the in-memory history die, and TurnComplete is never sent for that turn. I found no test that asserts this behaviour. A grep for "Interrupted" in the crates turned up only these sites in direct.rs. Two details differ from the report. The streaming path's Interrupt also bails "Interrupted" and lands in turn_error, which reaches TurnComplete{error}; it is graceful but still surfaces "Interrupted" as an error. I did not check how the app reacts to Exited, so the "next message starts a new session from a recap" part is inferred. The core claim holds: Stop during a tool or permission prompt ends the whole session instead of the turn.

I could not run the app, so this rests on reading the control flow. I traced Stop from the app to the direct-API session. The app's Stop handler sends Command::Interrupt. If the direct session is in a tool call, the interrupt arrives in one of two places: ask_permission, or the commands.recv() arm of run_bash_command. Both bail!("Interrupted"). execute_tool does not catch it. It propagates the error with `?` in the bash arm and the permission arms. In run(), the call `execute_tool(...).await?` sits inside the tool-call loop and outside the `match result { Err(e) => ... }` that handles streaming errors. The `?` therefore returns Err from run() and ends the session, not just the turn. supervise then sends AgentEvent::Error("Interrupted") followed by Exited. In workspace.rs, Exited with turn_started set takes the crash path. The Error event pushes Item::Error {text: "Interrupted"} and sets turn_error, so no "stopped unexpectedly" row is added. The run state becomes Failed and live.commands becomes None. TurnComplete{error: "Interrupted"} is never sent, so the app's graceful path (a "Interrupted" Notice and RunState::Idle) is skipped. The next message needs a new session, and the in-memory history is lost. The streaming path handles the same interrupt properly: its Err arm pops history and sets turn_error, which ends only the turn. The reporter's quoted code matches the current file, with minor line drift. No test asserts the session-ending behaviour. The only execute_tool tests call it for write_file, read_file and edit_file, and none exercise an interrupt. Shutdown during a permission prompt ending the session is expected and harmless.

findings.title: A failed model call after a tool result corrupts history; every later OpenAI request is rejected
findings.summary: On any error in the tool loop `history.pop()` is meant to remove the user's message, but on the second or later iteration the last entry is a `role: tool` result. Popping it leaves an assistant message with `tool_calls` that has no matching tool reply, and OpenAI (and compatible providers) reject such a conversation with 400 on every subsequent request, so the thread's session is unusable until it is relaunched.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenAI direct session. Model calls read_file (iteration 1): history = [user, assistant{tool_calls:[c1]}, tool{c1}]. Iteration 2 request fails (user hits Stop while it streams -> keep_command bails; or a 429/5xx/timeout). Err branch pops tool{c1}; history now ends with assistant{tool_calls:[c1]}. Next user prompt pushes user -> request messages [..., assistant{tool_calls}, user] -> OpenAI 400 "An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'"; openai_turn's retry without `tools` sends the same messages and fails too; the new user message is popped again. Every following prompt fails the same way.
findings.evidence: direct.rs:313-320: `Err(e) => { history.pop(); if let Some(crate::limits::LimitError(limit)) = e.downcast_ref() { ... } turn_error.get_or_insert_with(|| format!("{e:#}")); break; }`. The tool loop pushes `history.push(json!({ "role": "assistant", "content": ..., "tool_calls": tool_calls_json }))` (direct.rs:255-259) and per call `history.push(json!({ "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": output }))` (direct.rs:298-302) before looping back to the next model request at line 220. keep_command (direct.rs:884-893) bails "Interrupted" on Interrupt during streaming (direct.rs:1152 `cmd = commands.recv() => keep_command(cmd, kept, shutdown)?`).
findings.suggested_fix: On error, truncate history back to the index recorded before the user message was pushed (or to just before the last assistant tool_calls entry), rather than popping one entry.

verdicts.reasoning: I read the loop in direct.rs lines 195-320 and openai_turn. The Err arm does an unconditional `history.pop()` that assumes the last entry is the user message. That holds only on iteration 1. After a tool iteration, the last entry is a `role: tool` message, because the assistant{tool_calls} message is pushed at ~256 and each tool result at ~298. An error on iteration 2 therefore pops a tool result and leaves the assistant{tool_calls} entry dangling. Nothing repairs or sanitizes history anywhere else: `history` is only pushed to and popped in these spots, and openai_turn copies it verbatim into `messages`. The 400-retry in openai_turn only drops `tools`, so it sends the same messages. Iteration 2 can fail through reachable paths. keep_command bails "Interrupted" on Command::Interrupt during send_request or streaming. 429/5xx and timeouts go through request_error. The dangling assistant{tool_calls} message then precedes the next user message, which OpenAI rejects with a 400 because the tool_call_ids have no tool replies. Every later prompt fails the same way, because the Err arm pops the new user message again and leaves the corrupt tail in place. No test or guard covers this, and the direct.rs file is unmodified in the working tree. One correction: with several tool calls in one assistant message, the pop removes only the last tool result, so the corruption is the same or worse. The Anthropic wire is unaffected, since it pushes `content` and breaks without a tool loop. Severity is medium-high: it needs a failure or Stop during a post-tool request, then the session is stuck until relaunch.

I read the current direct.rs. The Err arm at line 313 calls `history.pop()` unconditionally. `openai_turn` takes `&[Value]` and never mutates history. On iteration 1 the last entry is the user message, so the pop is correct there. On iteration 2 or later, the Ok arm has already pushed the assistant message with tool_calls (line 256) and one tool message per call (line 298), so the last entry is a tool message. The Err arm then pops that tool message and leaves the assistant tool_calls message unanswered. Nothing repairs history afterwards. The loop breaks, turn_error is reported, and the same `history` Vec persists for the whole session, so the next Prompt pushes a user message after the dangling assistant tool_calls. `openai_turn` builds its messages as `[system] + history` with no sanitising, so the next request carries an assistant message whose tool_calls have no tool replies. The OpenAI chat API rejects that with a 400, and the 400 fallback only drops `tools` and resends the same messages. Interrupt during send_request or the stream goes through keep_command, which bails "Interrupted", so the Stop path reaches the Err arm. I did not run a live request, so the 400 itself rests on documented OpenAI behaviour. With several tool calls in one assistant message, one pop leaves more than one tool message missing or leaves the history oddly shaped, which is worse. One detail the reporter got slightly wrong: the Err arm also runs on the shutdown path, but that session ends anyway, so it doesn't matter.

findings.title: A message sent to a never-loaded thread is duplicated in the store when the thread is later opened
findings.summary: send_as/ensure_session never load a thread's history first, so a send from an off-screen path (phone remote_send, an agent's send_to_thread after a relaunch) pushes and persists items onto an empty live transcript with loaded=false. When the user then opens the thread, load_for_view treats every item in that live transcript as 'arrived while loading', appends it again after the stored rows (which already contain it) with fresh ids, and persists the copies.
findings.failure_scenario: Relaunch Trek (live is empty). Parent thread P, started in an earlier run, is resumed and its agent calls send_to_thread to child C it started last run; or the phone posts a Send to any listed thread it hasn't opened in this run. send_as(C): holds_messages is false (no live entry), ensure_session creates the live entry, live.items.push(User) (3340), persist_items appends the row to the DB (3378). The agent answers; Assistant and TurnEnd rows are persisted too. User clicks C in the sidebar: navigate -> load_for_view; `l.loaded || l.loading` is false so the async read runs; in the callback `arrived = replace(&mut live.items, Transcript::stored(rows))` is [User, Assistant, TurnEnd] (all already in rows), each is pushed again as a new unsaved item (2580-2582), and `!arrived.is_empty()` triggers persist_items (2587-2588), which INSERTs the three rows a second time. The transcript shows the exchange twice, permanently. (The sync variant ensure_loaded at 2616 has the sibling problem: it overwrites live.items with stored rows without shifting live.streaming/reasoning, so a turn still streaming on such a thread writes deltas into whatever item sits at that index in the history.)
findings.evidence: workspace.rs 3267-3279: `if self.holds_messages(&id) { ... }` -- holds_queue only checks `l.loading || l.preparing || l.removing`, never `!l.loaded`. 3338-3340: `let live = self.live.entry(id.clone()).or_default(); ... live.items.push(Item::User {...})`. 3378: `self.persist_items(&id, cx);` with 4339 `filter(|l| !l.loading)` passing. 2522: `if self.live.get(id).is_some_and(|l| l.loaded || l.loading) || self.thread(id).is_none() { return self.ensure_loaded(id, cx); }`. 2574: `let arrived = std::mem::replace(&mut live.items, Transcript::stored(rows));` 2580-2582: `for item in arrived.iter().cloned() { live.items.push(item); }` 2587-2588: `if live.end_orphaned_calls() || !arrived.is_empty() { this.persist_items(&id, cx); }`. transcript.rs 97-101: push() allocates a new id and marks it unsaved; store.rs 1420-1421 append_rows inserts after MAX(seq). Callers without ensure_loaded: remote.rs 682-699 (`remote_send` -> `self.send_to`), lineage.rs 473-487 (`send_to_thread` -> `self.send_as`, `follows` at 332-338 accepts threads from the store).
findings.suggested_fix: In send_as (and ensure_session) call load_for_view/ensure_loaded first and treat `!loaded` like `loading` in holds_queue so the message queues until the history is in; alternatively in load_for_view only re-append items whose ids are unsaved (Transcript::changes().appended) rather than the whole previous transcript.

verdicts.reasoning: I traced the code paths on disk. send_as only checks holds_messages. holds_queue tests `loading || preparing || removing`, never `!loaded`, so a thread with no live entry passes. ensure_session does not load history. Neither do the listed callers. send_to_thread (lineage.rs) calls follows(), which reads the store but does not load, and then send_as. remote_send calls send_to directly. The phone's `when_loaded` helper, which does load, is used for other requests but not for Send. send_as then creates a default Live (loaded=false, loading=false) and pushes the User item. persist_items only filters on `!l.loading`, so save_transcript runs and append_rows inserts the row after MAX(seq). Events from the session also persist the Assistant and TurnEnd rows the same way. When the user later opens the thread, navigate calls load_for_view. Its guard `l.loaded || l.loading` is false, so the async read runs. The callback replaces live.items with Transcript::stored(rows). That set already contains the rows persisted earlier. It treats the old live.items as `arrived`, clones each one, and push() assigns a fresh id and marks it unsaved. It then calls persist_items because `!arrived.is_empty()`. That inserts the rows a second time. I found no dedupe and no test that asserts this behaviour. The result is a duplicated exchange in the DB and in the UI. It is corruption rather than loss, and it needs a specific sequence: an off-screen send to a thread not loaded this run, followed by the user opening it. The reporter's parenthetical about ensure_loaded and streaming indexes is plausible but I did not verify it. It is not needed for the main claim.

I did not run a test. Adding one would mean editing the repo, and the tests would take minutes to build. I traced the code on disk instead, and every link in the chain holds. (1) send_as (workspace.rs 3265-3390) never calls ensure_loaded or load_for_view. Its only early exit for a not-yet-loaded thread is holds_messages -> holds_queue (3405), which tests only `l.loading || l.preparing || l.removing`, worktree-missing, and agent_updates.held. It never tests `!l.loaded`. (2) For a thread with no live entry, ensure_session and `self.live.entry(..).or_default()` create a live entry with loaded=false and empty items, and `live.items.push(Item::User{..})` follows (3340). persist_items (4345) is guarded only by `!l.loading`, so it appends the User row to the DB and mark_saved runs. (3) Events from the agent add Assistant and TurnEnd rows to the same live transcript. apply_events has no loaded/loading guard (my rg for loaded|loading in its body found nothing). (4) Opening the thread: navigate -> load_for_view (2528). The guard `l.loaded || l.loading` is false, so the async read runs. The callback calls `mem::replace(&mut live.items, Transcript::stored(rows))`, and `rows` already includes the User/Assistant/TurnEnd rows persisted earlier. Then `for item in arrived.iter().cloned() { live.items.push(item) }` runs. Transcript::push (transcript.rs 97-104) gives each item a new id and marks it unsaved. `!arrived.is_empty()` then triggers persist_items, and append_rows INSERTs them again after MAX(seq). The exchange is stored twice and shown twice. The load_for_view comment ('arrived while it was read') shows it was written for the case where the thread was loading and messages were held, not for a send that already persisted. The agent-side path is reachable. send_to_thread (lineage.rs 473-487) calls send_as with no ensure_loaded. `follows` accepts threads from the store, so after a relaunch a child thread C from the previous run has no live entry. The phone path is weaker. remote_send calls send_to directly, but the phone usually reads the thread first, and that read goes through the helper at remote.rs 866-870, which calls ensure_loaded. Only a blind send to a thread not opened this run would hit it. I did not confirm the sync-variant side claim about live.streaming/reasoning, but it is secondary.

findings.title: `script/capture.sh ios/<suite>` silently captures nothing because capture-list.sh cd's before resolving relative paths
findings.summary: capture-list.sh does `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` (into ios/) before using its manifest and output arguments. capture.sh passes both relative to the repo root (`media/ios/store.list`, `dist/media/ios/store`). The manifest is therefore looked up as ios/media/ios/store.list, which does not exist. The `grep | while` pipeline returns the while loop's status, so the script exits 0 with no work done.
findings.failure_scenario: `script/capture.sh ios/store` (or the example in capture-list.sh's own header, run from the repo root) prints `grep: media/ios/store.list: No such file or directory`, builds and captures nothing, creates an empty ios/dist/media/ios/store, and then capture.sh prints `published → dist/media/ios/store` and exits 0. I reproduced this with `ios/scripts/capture-list.sh media/ios/store.list dist/zz-test`, which gave the grep error, rc=0 and a stray ios/dist directory (I removed it).
findings.evidence: capture-list.sh:12-16: `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` / `MANIFEST=${1:?manifest}; OUTDIR=${2:-screenshots}` / `mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"` / `grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$MANIFEST" | while IFS= read -r line; do`; capture.sh:142-143: `ios/scripts/capture-list.sh "$file" "$OUT/$suite"` / `say "published → $OUT/$suite"`
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve MANIFEST and OUTDIR to absolute paths (`${1:A}` or `$(cd ...)`) before the cd. Add `set -o pipefail` or check `[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]`.

verdicts.reasoning: Read capture-list.sh and capture.sh on disk. capture.sh does `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` to the repo root and sets OUT=${OUT:-dist/media}. run_ios checks that media/ios/$suite.list exists relative to the repo root, then calls `ios/scripts/capture-list.sh "$file" "$OUT/$suite"` with both paths relative. capture-list.sh runs `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`, which lands in ios/, before it reads $1 and $2. ios/media does not exist (only the repo-root media/ios/store.list does), so grep fails on the manifest. I did not re-run it, but the code path is unambiguous. No guard or test covers it. The header example (media/ios/store.list from the repo root) has the same problem. Absolute paths would work, but capture.sh does not pass any.

Read capture-list.sh: it cd's to ios/ before using relative MANIFEST/OUTDIR. capture.sh run_ios passes media/ios/store.list and dist/media/<suite>, both relative to the repo root; capture.sh does cd to the repo root at line 20, and OUT defaults to relative dist/media. ios/media does not exist, so grep fails. Without pipefail, the pipeline status is that of the while loop (0), and set -e does not trigger. findings.title: Any command received while a bash tool runs kills the command and fails the turn as Interrupted
findings.summary: run_bash_command's select! treats every incoming Command as a stop: it kills the child, queues the command via keep_command (which returns Ok for Prompt/SetModel/SetHandHolding/SetModes), and then unconditionally bails "Interrupted". The streaming paths use keep_command to keep going; this one does not. Combined with the `?` propagation above, a steer message typed during `cargo test` ends the whole session.
findings.failure_scenario: Direct session runs bash `cargo test` (model's tool call). The user types a follow-up message (steer), or changes the access level in the thread header (SetHandHolding), or picks another model. commands.recv() fires at line 637 -> `child.kill()` kills the test run -> keep_command returns Ok (command queued) -> `bail!("Interrupted")` -> execute_tool Err -> session exits with Error("Interrupted"). The user never asked to stop. Also, `child.kill()` only kills the `sh` (not spawned in a process group), so `sh -c "cargo build && cargo test"` leaves cargo running.
findings.evidence: direct.rs:636-641: `cmd = commands.recv() => { let _ = child.kill().await; keep_command(cmd, kept, shutdown)?; bail!("Interrupted") }`. direct.rs:884-893 keep_command: `Ok(cmd) => { kept.push_back(cmd); Ok(()) }` for non-control commands. direct.rs:576-583 spawns via `trek_core::procs::async_command("sh").arg("-c").arg(command)...spawn()` with no spawn_group. Compare direct.rs:1052 and 1152 where the same `keep_command(cmd, kept, shutdown)?` is used to keep streaming.
findings.suggested_fix: Loop on commands.recv() inside the select and only kill/bail when keep_command returns Err (Interrupt/Shutdown); spawn the shell with crate::spawn_group and terminate the group.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced the path from the app's steer dispatch down to run_bash_command and then back out to the session supervisor.

1. direct.rs:636-641 matches the quote. Any Command received by commands.recv() makes the select! arm kill the child, call keep_command, and then bail!("Interrupted").
2. keep_command (884-893) returns Ok for Prompt, SetModel, SetHandHolding and SetModes. It only bails for Interrupt, Shutdown or a closed channel. So for a steer message the `?` does nothing and the unconditional bail! still fires.
3. execute_tool line 499 propagates the error with `?`. The caller at about line 271-282 also uses `.await?` inside run()'s outer loop. That `?` is not the `Err(e)` arm that turn_error handles, because it sits in the tool-call loop and not in the turn-result match. So the error leaves run() entirely.
4. In lib.rs, supervise() turns an Err from run() into AgentEvent::Error("Interrupted"), followed by Exited. The whole direct session therefore ends.
5. The app does send a Prompt to a running session as a steer. workspace.rs:3355 says "A message sent while a turn runs steers that turn", and it calls dispatch(Command::Prompt). dispatch uses tx.try_send, so the command reaches commands.recv() while bash is running.
6. No test asserts this. The inline tests only cover write_file, read_file and edit_file. The scenario.rs interrupt test expects a real Interrupt to end with "Interrupted" and the session to stay usable ("session still usable"). That is not what happens for bash on the Direct path, because the `?` kills the session.

The process-group claim is plausible too. The spawn is plain async_command("sh") with no group, and child.kill() signals only sh. It is a minor extra.

Correction on severity: even a genuine Interrupt during bash ends the session, not just the turn, because the `?` bypasses turn_error handling. Steering, a model change or an access-level change also kills a long bash command and ends the session.

I confirmed this by reading the code. I did not run a test or a scratch repro. In run_bash_command (direct.rs ~636-641), any Command from commands.recv() kills the child, calls keep_command, and then does an unconditional bail!("Interrupted"). keep_command returns Ok for Prompt, SetModel, SetHandHolding and SetModes, so the `?` does not stop first. The bail then returns Err from run_bash_command. execute_tool (line 499) propagates it with `?`. The caller in run() (lines 271-282) also uses `.await?` on execute_tool, and it sits outside the Err(e) arm that sets turn_error. So the error leaves direct::run entirely. supervise() in lib.rs sends AgentEvent::Error("Interrupted") and then Exited, so the session ends and the in-memory history is lost. A steer prompt, a SetHandHolding change or a SetModel change while a bash tool runs kills the command and ends the session. The same path means even a plain user Interrupt during bash ends the session instead of just ending the turn. The streaming paths use keep_command and carry on, so this path is inconsistent with them. No test asserts the behaviour. The child is spawned with plain async_command("sh") and no process group, so child.kill() only kills sh. Grandchildren such as cargo can survive, though I did not verify that part. The app dispatches Command::Prompt and SetHandHolding to the live session at any time (workspace.rs:2791, 3373, 5924), so the trigger is reachable.

findings.title: Selections and paths with '+', '&', '#' or '?' are corrupted between the editor extension and Trek
findings.summary: The extension builds the query with URLSearchParams and hands a vscode.Uri to env.openExternal. VS Code's Uri.parse percent-decodes the query and openExternal re-emits it as encodeURI(uri.toString(true)), which leaves '+', '&' and '=' bare and double-encodes '#'/'?'; Trek's deep_link::parse then splits on '&' and decode() turns '+' into a space, so the text that lands in the composer (or the file path opened) is not what was selected.
findings.failure_scenario: In VS Code/Cursor select `if (a && b) { i + 1; }` and run "Ask Trek about selection". URLSearchParams encodes it as `if+(a+%26%26+b)+%7B+i+%2B+1%3B+%7D`; Uri.parse decodes to `if (a && b) { i + 1; }` with spaces as '+': `if+(a+&&+b)+{+i+++1;+}`; encodeURI keeps '+', '&', '=' and re-encodes only '%', '{', '}' → Trek receives `...&selection=if+(a+&&+b)+%7B+i+++1;+%7D`. deep_link::parse splits the query on '&', so the selection becomes `if (a ` (the rest becomes empty/unknown keys and is dropped). Without the '&&', `i + 1` arrives as `i   1` (every '+' becomes a space); `#[derive(Debug)]` arrives as `%23[derive(Debug)]`. Likewise "Open in Trek" on `/Users/me/c++/main.cpp` sends path `/Users/me/c++/main.cpp` → Trek decodes to `/Users/me/c  /main.cpp`, which fails the trust check (prompts) and then opens a nonexistent path.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the already-encoded string to openExternal (VS Code preserves a string argument as-is: the `n?r=o` branch), e.g. `vscode.env.openExternal(`trek://${command}?${params}`)` — or, to stay within the typed API, encode each value so it survives the decode→encodeURI round trip (e.g. base64url the path/selection and have deep_link::decode accept that), and stop treating '+' as a space in deep_link::decode once the extension no longer emits it.

verdicts.reasoning: I read extension/extension.js and deep_link.rs. I then checked the installed Cursor bundle, which shares VS Code's extension host. The extension passes a vscode.Uri, not a string, to openExternal. In extensionHostProcess.js, `openUri(e,n)` sets `a` (the original string) only when `typeof e=="string"`. With a Uri argument `a` is undefined, so `$openUri(e,undefined,n)` runs. In MainThreadWindow `$openUri`, `t&&...` is false, so the target stays a Uri, not the original string. `_doOpenExternal` then computes `r=encodeURI(i.toString(!0))`, because the string-preserving branch needs `typeof e=="string"`. Uri.parse percent-decodes the query. toString(true) emits it undecoded-as-is. encodeURI leaves `& + = # ?` alone in what it emits (`#` and `?` are left bare too). So `%26` from URLSearchParams becomes a bare `&`, and `%2B` becomes a bare `+`. Trek's `parse` splits on `&` and `decode` maps `+` to a space. I found no earlier validation or guard, and no test covers this path. The existing tests only use hand-written `%20`/`%3D` URLs, so none asserts this behaviour is intended. The reporter's detail on '#' and '?' being double-encoded is shaky: encodeURI leaves `#` and `?` as they are, and it only escapes `%`. The `+` and `&` corruption is solid, and so is the failing path with `c++`. Passing the URL as a string would avoid it, since the string branch preserves the original encoding.

I read extension/extension.js and crates/trek-app/src/deep_link.rs on disk. Both match the reporter's quotes. I then checked the installed VS Code bundles.

- extensionHostProcess.js: `openUri(t,e)` only sets the original string `n` when the caller passed a string. The extension passes a `vscode.Uri`, so `n` is undefined and `$openUri(t, undefined, e)` is called.
- workbench.desktop.main.js: `$openUri` then uses the Uri object. `_resolveExternalUriOpenTarget` takes the `encodeURI(i.toString(!0))` branch, because `typeof o=="string"` is false.
- `Uri.parse` percent-decodes the query. `toString(true)` emits it unencoded, and `encodeURI` leaves `&`, `+`, `=`, `#` and `?` alone.

I simulated that pipeline in node. For path `/Users/me/c++/main.cpp` and selection `if (a && b) { i + 1; }` it produced `path=/Users/me/c++/main.cpp&selection=if+(a+&&+b)+%7B+i+++1;+%7D`. In `deep_link::parse` the query is split on `&` before decoding. The selection is therefore cut at the `&&` (it becomes `if (a `), and the rest is dropped as empty or unknown keys. Without `&&`, `decode()` turns every `+` into a space, so `i + 1` becomes `i   1` and the path becomes `/Users/me/c  /main.cpp`. The existing tests only cover `%XX` input, so none of them asserts this behaviour as intended.

I did not run Trek's `parse` itself. Its logic is plain from the source.

findings.title: Popover closed by the task vanishing leaves ws.overlay_open stuck true
findings.summary: In sync(), when the shown thread changes, or `shown` becomes None because the last background task ended, `self.output` is cleared without calling `self.overlay(false, cx)`. The later `if let Some(open) = &self.output` block, which does call overlay(false), is then skipped because output is already None. The popover is torn down without on_open_change firing, so Workspace::overlay_open stays true.
findings.failure_scenario: The user opens a dev server's output popover (bg-task) and presses Stop in the card, or the server exits on its own. `read()` now returns None, so shown=None. The first `if` sets output=None and the overlay is never released. The strip disappears, but overlay_open stays true. Native views stay hidden for as long as it is true: artifact/mod.rs:1040 hides artifact web views, panels/mod.rs:242 hides the browser, and ide/editor_group.rs:211 hides the editor previews. They come back only when some other surface (palette, composer, image preview) opens and closes. The existing test tests/background.rs:86-93 does exactly this click-then-Stop sequence and never asserts overlay_open is false afterwards.
findings.evidence: background_strip.rs:159-162: `if shown.as_ref().map(|s| &s.thread) != self.shown.as_ref().map(|s| &s.thread) { self.expanded = false; self.output = None; }` followed by :163-168 `if let Some(open) = &self.output && shown.as_ref().is_none_or(|s| !s.rows.iter().any(|r| r.id == *open)) { self.output = None; self.overlay(false, cx); }`. With the first block having already cleared output, the second can only run when the thread is the same and other tasks remain.
findings.suggested_fix: In the thread-changed branch, call self.overlay(false, cx) when self.output.take().is_some(). Better, compute `had = self.output.is_some()` before any clearing and call overlay(false) once after the clearing if had && self.output.is_none(). Add an overlay_open assertion to tests/background.rs after the Stop click.

verdicts.reasoning: I read sync(), overlay(), set_output() and the Popover wiring. The quoted code is accurate. When the shown thread differs from self.shown's thread, sync() sets self.output = None at line 159-162 and does not call overlay(false). The next block (163-168) is the only place in sync() that releases the overlay, and it requires self.output to be Some. So it is skipped. When the last task ends, read() returns None because rows is empty. The thread comparison is then None against Some, so the first block fires and output is cleared without releasing. The strip then renders nothing, so the Popover with on_open_change is no longer in the tree. gpui-base popover.rs has no Drop impl, and on_open_change only fires from the popover's own state, so no callback releases it. set_output is the only other release path and is not triggered. Nothing else clears ws.overlay_open on this path: the other writers are the palette, composer, image preview, panel drag end and main_window_closed. The effect is real: overlay_open stays true, which hides the artifact web views, the browser panel (menu_open) and the editor previews until another surface opens and closes. The test at tests/background.rs:86-93 does the click-then-Stop sequence and never asserts overlay_open, so no test treats the stuck state as intended. The thread-switch half of the claim holds too, since output is cleared without a release. I did not run the app. This is a code-trace verdict.

I read sync() and overlay() in the working tree. I did not run a test, because a trek-app test build is slow and I may not edit the repo. The evidence is correctly quoted. When shown becomes None, or the thread changes, the first `if` sets self.output = None without calling overlay(false). The second `if let Some(open) = &self.output` is then skipped, so overlay(false) never runs on that path. The only other callers that release the overlay are set_output, which runs on popover open-change events, and set_hidden. Neither fires when the strip's rows vanish. The Popover for that row is simply no longer rendered, so on_open_change is not triggered by user interaction. In the tests the strip is created with Scope::Main (root.rs:122), so overlay() does write ws.overlay_open. Opening the popover via bg-task click goes through set_output(Some) and sets overlay_open = true. Pressing Stop (or the server exiting) empties the background list, so read() returns None and the shown thread goes from Some to None. The first `if` then runs and the overlay is never released. The existing test at tests/background.rs:86-93 does click then Stop and never asserts overlay_open afterwards, so no test marks this as intended. I found no other reset. overlay_open is cleared elsewhere only by a panel drag ending (root.rs:1129), main_window_closed, and other surfaces closing (palette, composer, image preview). Consumers do read the flag: panels/mod.rs:242, artifact/mod.rs:1040 and ide/editor_group.rs:211. Severity is medium rather than high because it is a transient hidden-native-view state that clears when some other overlay opens and closes.

findings.title: Install-Trek.ps1's download fallback points at an asset name releases never have
findings.summary: When no local trek.exe is found, the installer downloads `releases/latest/download/Trek-windows-x86_64.zip`. release.ps1 publishes `Trek-<version>-windows-x86_64.zip`, and no unversioned asset exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.failure_scenario: A user downloads only Install-Trek.ps1 or install.bat, with no trek.exe beside it or in the current directory, and runs it. Find-TrekSources returns null and Invoke-WebRequest gets a 404. With `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` the GUI shows "Error: ... (404) Not Found" and Trek cannot be installed through this path.
findings.evidence: Install-Trek.ps1:65 `$zipUrl = "https://github.com/dokyit/Trek/releases/latest/download/Trek-windows-x86_64.zip"`; release.ps1:90 `$Name = "Trek-$Version-$Platform.zip"`; docs/RELEASING.md:231 `Trek-<version>-windows-x86_64.zip`
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the asset through the GitHub API (`gh`/REST `releases/latest`, pick the asset matching `Trek-*-windows-x86_64.zip`), or publish a stable unversioned alias asset.

verdicts.reasoning: I opened script/Install-Trek.ps1 and found line 65 as quoted. The fallback branch of Install-TrekFiles runs only when Find-TrekSources returns null, meaning no trek.exe beside the script, in the current directory, or in the target\release paths. That branch downloads releases/latest/download/Trek-windows-x86_64.zip. release.ps1:89-90 builds the asset name as "Trek-$Version-$Platform.zip", with the version in it. RELEASING.md, README.md and script/lib/notes.sh all name the versioned asset. I grepped the repo for any unversioned "Trek-windows-x86_64" and found only the installer's own two uses (the URL and the temp zip name). Nothing uploads an alias with that name. GitHub's latest/download/<name> needs an exact asset name, so the request returns 404. $ErrorActionPreference is "Stop", so Invoke-WebRequest aborts the install. No guard or test makes this intended. The only unverified part is the GUI wording of the error, which doesn't change the outcome. The impact is narrow because the primary Windows path is Trek-Setup-x86_64.exe or the zip. install.bat just calls the same script.

I read script/Install-Trek.ps1 and searched the whole repo for the asset name. Line 65 is quoted accurately. The fallback branch (lines 63-74) runs when Find-TrekSources finds no trek.exe in $PSScriptRoot, the current directory, or ..\target\release or ..\target\x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\release. Nothing guards it. script/install.bat only forwards to Install-Trek.ps1, so a user with just the .ps1 or .bat file reaches the branch. release.ps1:89-90 names the zip `Trek-$Version-windows-x86_64.zip`. Its upload step (lines 308-322) sends the versioned zip, its .minisig, the installer `Trek-Setup-x86_64.exe` and the channel manifest. It also deletes other `Trek-*-windows-x86_64.zip*` assets. The release-windows.yml workflow calls release.ps1 and uses the same versioned name. The only hits for the unversioned `Trek-windows-x86_64.zip` are Install-Trek.ps1 lines 65-66. No test asserts the behaviour. GitHub's /releases/latest/download/<name> URL needs an exact asset name, so the unversioned URL returns 404. With $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop", Invoke-WebRequest then throws. I did not run it on Windows. The case rests on the code and the naming being unambiguous. It only affects the standalone-script case, since the local-source path works. The Setup.exe and the versioned zip are other install routes, which limits the impact.

findings.title: Registered uninstaller ignores a custom install folder and reports success without removing it
findings.summary: The installer lets the user pick any folder (Browse, or -InstallDir). The Add/Remove Programs entry's UninstallString and QuietUninstallString run Uninstall-Trek.ps1 without `-InstallDir`. The uninstaller defaults to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trek.
findings.failure_scenario: The user installs to D:\Apps\Trek and later clicks Uninstall in Settings. The script kills Trek, deletes the shortcuts and the registry key, finds %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trek missing, and says "Trek has been successfully uninstalled". D:\Apps\Trek is left behind with all its binaries, and the uninstall entry is gone so it can't be retried from Settings.
findings.evidence: Install-Trek.ps1:118 `-Name "UninstallString" -Value "powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File `"$uninstallerScript`""` and :119 (QuietUninstallString, `-Silent`, also without -InstallDir); Uninstall-Trek.ps1:22 `[string]$InstallDir = (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\Trek")`
findings.suggested_fix: Append `-InstallDir \"$targetDir\"` to both registry strings, or default `$InstallDir` to `$PSScriptRoot` in Uninstall-Trek.ps1.

verdicts.reasoning: I read Install-Trek.ps1 and Uninstall-Trek.ps1 on disk. The installer takes $InstallDir from the -InstallDir parameter or the Browse textbox. It passes the chosen folder as $targetDir to Install-TrekFiles, which copies Uninstall-Trek.ps1 into it, and to Register-WindowsUninstall. That function writes UninstallString and QuietUninstallString with only -File "<targetDir>\Uninstall-Trek.ps1" (plus -Silent for the quiet one). Neither string passes -InstallDir. Uninstall-Trek.ps1 declares $InstallDir with a default of %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trek and never reads $PSScriptRoot or the registry's InstallLocation value. Step 5 removes the uninstall registry key unconditionally. Step 6 is guarded by `if (Test-Path $InstallDir)`, so a missing default folder skips deletion silently. The script then prints "Trek has been uninstalled" and, if not Silent, shows the "successfully uninstalled" message box. I found no test or other guard. For a custom folder, the files are left behind and the Settings entry is gone. The reporter's quoted evidence matches the code. The only imprecision is that "Programs\Trek" is a default, not an error: if the default folder happens to exist, the wrong folder would be deleted instead.

I read both scripts on disk. Install-Trek.ps1 accepts any -InstallDir and lets the user pick one through the Browse dialog. findings.title: A sub-agent started from a no-project thread registers the scratch chat folder as a project

A no-project thread is made with `(!chat).then_some(cwd)` at workspace.rs:3196, so no project is created for it, and lineage.rs:293 goes through `project_dir`, which also filters chat dirs. verdicts.reasoning: I traced it in order. (1) A no-project thread is made in make_thread (workspace.rs:3196) with create_thread(None,...), and then thread.cwd = Some(chat dir) is set afterwards. So the parent's cwd is a chats/ scratch folder and its project_id is None. (2) start_subagent (orchestrate.rs:397) passes parent.cwd.as_deref() straight into store.create_thread. findings.title: Auto mode's safe-command check lets destructive shell commands run without approval
findings.summary: Under HandHolding::Auto a bash call skips the permission prompt when the command starts with a listed prefix and contains none of `; & | >`. Command substitution, newlines, and destructive flags of listed tools all pass: `echo $(rm -rf ~)`, `cat \`curl ... \``, `ls .\nrm -rf ~`, `find . -delete`, `find . -exec rm -rf {} +`, `git branch -D main`. The command is run verbatim with `sh -c`, so all of these execute silently.
findings.failure_scenario: Thread on a direct provider at Auto ("risky actions are checked"). The model (or repo content via prompt injection) emits bash `find . -name '*.rs' -delete` or `echo $(git reset --hard origin/main)`. is_safe_command: no `;&|>`, starts with "find "/"echo " -> true -> need_ask=false -> run_bash_command executes it in the project with no card shown. Files are deleted/overwritten without the user ever being asked.
findings.evidence: direct.rs:373-390: `if trimmed.contains(';') || trimmed.contains('&') || trimmed.contains('|') || trimmed.contains('>') { return false; } let safe_prefixes = ["git status", ..., "ls", "cat", "head", "tail", "grep", "rg", "find", "fd", "pwd", "which", "echo", "wc", "stat", "file"]; safe_prefixes.iter().any(|p| trimmed == *p || trimmed.starts_with(&format!("{p} ")))`. direct.rs:483-486: `HandHolding::Auto => !is_safe_command(command) && !allowed_for_session.contains(command)`. direct.rs:576-579 runs it as `sh -c <command>`. The test safe_command_checks (direct.rs:1515-1523) only covers `;` and `&&`.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject `$(`, backticks, newlines and `<`; and treat `find`/`fd` with -delete/-exec/-x, and `git branch` with -D/-d, as unsafe (or whitelist read-only subcommands by argument rather than by prefix).

verdicts.reasoning: I read is_safe_command (direct.rs:373-390), the bash branch of execute_tool (about line 473-501), and run_bash_command. The quoted evidence matches the file. In Auto mode, need_ask is `!is_safe_command(command) && !allowed_for_session.contains(command)`. If is_safe_command returns true, no ask_permission call happens and run_bash_command runs immediately. is_safe_command only rejects `; & | >` and then does a prefix match, so it does not reject `$(`, backticks, newlines, `<`, or destructive flags of listed tools. I traced `echo $(rm -rf ~)`: it contains none of the four banned characters, and it starts with "echo ", so it returns true. `find . -name '*.rs' -delete` and `find . -exec rm -rf {} +` pass the same way, and so does `git branch -D main` ("git branch " prefix). Newline injection such as `ls .\nrm -rf ~` also passes, because only `;` is checked and not `\n`. The command goes to `sh -c` unmodified. The only test, safe_command_checks (about line 1525-1531), checks `;` and `&&`, plus basic positives. It does not assert that substitution or `find -delete` count as safe, so nothing marks this as intended. Auto is meant to check risky actions, and the prefix allowlist is clearly meant to cover read-only commands. The reported scenario holds. Reachability depends on a direct-provider thread in Auto mode, where the model or injected repo content picks the command. I did not run the code, only traced it statically.

findings.title: remote_send leaves the Mac's follow-up setting changed when a photo can't be saved
findings.summary: remote_send overrides settings.general.follow_up with the phone's per-message mode before calling save_uploads, and the `?` on save_uploads returns early past the line that restores it, so a failed photo upload permanently flips the Mac's Steer/Queue setting in memory (and it is written to disk by the next save_settings).
findings.failure_scenario: Mac setting is Follow-up = Queue. Phone sends a message to a working thread with mode: "steer" and an attached image that fails save_uploads (not JPEG/PNG magic bytes, decoded size > 10 MB, or the snapshots dir can't be created). remote_send returns Err at line 698; settings.general.follow_up stays Steer. Every later follow-up typed on the Mac (and every phone send without an explicit mode) now steers the running turn instead of queueing; the next save_settings from any settings change persists the flipped value.
findings.suggested_fix: Call save_uploads before touching the setting, or better, pass the mode straight through: `self.send_as(&req.thread_id, text, images, req.mode.map(|m| match m { Steer => FollowUp::Steer, Queue => FollowUp::Queue }), cx)` and drop the save/restore of settings.general.follow_up entirely.

verdicts.reasoning: I read remote_send on disk (remote.rs:681-701). The quoted code is accurate. `before` is saved, `settings.general.follow_up` is overwritten when `req.mode` is Some, and then `save_uploads(&req.images)?` runs before the restore line. If it errors, the function returns early and `self.settings.general.follow_up = before` is never reached. Nothing restores the setting by other means, such as a guard or a closure. I checked that save_uploads can fail on attacker or phone-controlled input. ImageUpload::decode (trek-remote/src/protocol.rs:319) returns Err for bad base64 or when the bytes are not JPEG/PNG. save_uploads also rejects decoded sizes over 10 MB and a failed create_dir_all or fs::write. So the flipped value does change later behaviour: Mac composer follow-ups (composer.rs:254, 2057) and phone sends without a mode. settings.general is also the struct that gets saved, so the next settings save persists the flip. I found no test in tests/remote.rs that asserts the leak is intended. The only follow_up assertion there (line 430) is about settings sync. findings.title: Closing a terminal tab never ends its shell: process and reader thread leak per tab
findings.summary: TerminalPanel has no Drop and never kills the child; the reader thread owns a dup of the pty master (reader) plus an Arc clone of the writer (another dup) and blocks in read() until the slave closes, which only happens when the shell exits. Dropping the panel therefore cannot hang up the shell (two master fds stay open), and the shell, idle at its prompt, keeps the thread blocked forever. The writer's EOT-on-drop (portable-pty's UnixMasterWriter::drop) that would have ended the shell never runs because the thread holds the last Arc.
findings.failure_scenario: Open the Terminal tool (zsh starts), press the tab's close button (RightPanel::close -> tabs.retain, no cleanup for View::Terminal) or terminal_dock's 'Kill terminal' / ide panel's kill_terminal (both only `self.terminals.remove(..)`). Afterwards `ps` still shows the zsh -l process and a trek-app thread blocked in read(); repeat ten times and ten shells remain until Trek quits. A terminal running `tail -f` behaves the same: once output arrives the pump breaks on the closed wake channel, then `child.wait()` blocks on a child that is never signalled.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement Drop for TerminalPanel (or an explicit `kill()` called from RightPanel::close, terminal_dock::kill_terminal and ide::panel::kill_terminal) that keeps the `Child` in the panel (e.g. Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Child>>>), calls `child.kill()` then `wait()`, and drops master/writer; alternatively don't move the writer into the reader thread on non-Windows so the EOT-on-drop path works.

verdicts.reasoning: I read spawn() and the struct in the working tree. TerminalPanel has no Drop and nothing in panels/ kills the child. The only child.kill() is in a test helper, which also does drop(pty.master), so the authors know an explicit kill is needed. The spawned thread owns the child, the cloned reader and a writer Arc clone. It sits in reader.read() and only exits on EOF or after a wake try_send fails on a closed channel, and both need shell output. Dropping the panel drops self.master and the Task (so rx closes), but the reader and writer fds are separate dups of the master, so the master is never hung up. The slave fd is dropped at the end of spawn, but the shell holds its own copy. An idle zsh therefore never gets SIGHUP or EOF, and the thread stays blocked. If output does arrive, pump breaks and the thread blocks in child.wait(), still holding the writer, so its EOT-on-drop never runs. The close paths only remove the entry: RightPanel::close does tabs.retain and handles just Browser and Simulator, and kill_terminal in terminal_dock.rs and ide/panel.rs does terminals.remove. I did not run the app. Impact is one shell plus one thread leaked per closed terminal until Trek quits, so medium to low severity.

I read the spawn code, which has no Drop impl and never kills or signals the child. The close paths are RightPanel::close, terminal_dock's kill_terminal and the ide panel's kill_terminal. None of them do any cleanup for a Terminal view: they only drop the entity. The only child.kill() in terminal.rs is inside a test helper at line 876. Real-world impact is a leaked process and thread per closed terminal tab, hence medium or low severity.

findings.title: Git panel can't show or count changes for non-ASCII file names (git quotes them, code treats the quoted form as the path)
findings.summary: snapshot() parses `git status --porcelain=v1` without -z and takes `line[3..]` verbatim. With core.quotePath (the default) git prints any path with bytes >= 0x80 as a C-quoted string, e.g. `"r\303\251sum\303\251.md"`. That quoted text becomes FileChange.path, so the row label is garbled, `git diff HEAD -- <quoted>` matches nothing (empty diff pane), and for an untracked file `cwd.join(&path)` doesn't exist so it reads as 0 lines / 'Binary, unreadable, or too large'.
findings.failure_scenario: In a project modify `résumé.md` (or any file with an accented/CJK name), open the Git tool. Verified in /tmp: `git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` prints ` M "r\303\251sum\303\251.md"` and `git diff HEAD -- "$(that path)"` outputs 0 bytes. The file list shows the escaped name, clicking it shows an empty diff, and an untracked such file shows +0. Same for the IDE Source Control view which reuses snapshot/file_diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall` (and `--numstat -z`) and split on NUL as explorer::git_marks does, or pass `-c core.quotePath=false`; handle the rename's second NUL-separated field.

It sets only fsmonitor, diff.noprefix, diff.mnemonicPrefix and splitIndex, and does not set core.quotepath=off. The only quotepath=off in the repo is in ide/git.rs, which is a different code path. I reproduced it in /tmp: git prints ` M "r\303\251sum\303\251.md"` by default and ` M résumé.md` with core.quotepath=off. The quoted string becomes FileChange.path. For tracked files it is passed as a pathspec to `git diff HEAD --`, which matches nothing, so the diff is empty. For untracked files `cwd.join(path)` does not exist, so untracked_text returns None and the diff pane shows 'Binary, unreadable, or too large'. findings.title: Agents page: Sign in / Install buttons stay on "Signing in…" / "Installing…" and inert forever after an abandoned or failed attempt
