findings.title: With the picture setting off, every step closes a picture the user asked to see
findings.summary: `record` closes the window on every step when `tools.background_pip` is false. The Show button in the working bar, the tray item and the palette entry stay available in that state and call `show()`, so a picture opened on request is closed again by the agent's next step.
findings.failure_scenario: The user turns off 'Show what they're doing'. An agent runs a background-use session, and the working bar shows 'Safari in the background · Show'. The user clicks Show and the picture opens, as the test 'Shown on request all the same' expects. The agent's next click, type or scroll arrives a second or two later. `record(.., picture = false, ..)` calls `self.close(cx)`, which takes the window and removes it. The picture vanishes almost at once, and the Show button cannot keep it open. The test only checks the state straight after `show()`, so it does not catch this.
findings.evidence: background_use.rs:138-142: `if !picture { self.close(cx); } else if !self.tucked { self.open(cx); }`. The tests/background_use.rs comment says 'Shown on request all the same'. working_bar.rs `behind_chip` shows Show whenever the session exists, regardless of `background_pip`.
findings.suggested_fix: When `picture` is false, do not call `close`. Just skip auto-opening, and leave any window the user opened on request until they tuck it or the sessions end.

verdicts.reasoning: I read background_use.rs record/show/close, the caller in workspace/orchestrate.rs, and the working-bar chip, palette and tray entry points. record() is quoted correctly. The caller passes picture = self.settings.tools.background_pip on every COMPUTER_ACTIVITY report. With the setting off, record() calls self.close(cx) on every step. close() takes self.window and removes it. Nothing in record() or close() checks whether the user asked for the picture. show() sets tucked = false and calls open(), but sets no state that record() reads when picture is false. behind_chip, the palette entry (shown whenever sessions is non-empty) and the tray item are not gated on background_pip. So the user can click Show, and the next agent step (clicks, typing and scrolls come about once a second) closes the picture again. The test the_picture_can_be_turned_off... only asserts showing() straight after show(), then reports a different step only after the 'no-such-thread' check, and never asserts the picture stays open across a later step. No test asserts the close-on-step behaviour as intended. The test comment says 'Shown on request all the same', which contradicts the picture vanishing a step later. The impact is small: the setting is off and the feature is a convenience window.

I read the code on disk and traced the path by reading. I did not run a test. The quoted lines are accurate. `record` runs `self.close(cx)` on every step when `picture` is false. `orchestrate.rs:248-249` passes `settings.tools.background_pip` into `record` on every computer-activity report. `behind_chip` in the working bar, the tray item (`toggle`) and the palette entry ("Show background use") all show whenever `sessions` is non-empty. None of them check `background_pip`. `show()` sets `tucked = false` and calls `open`. The next `record` with `picture = false` hits the first branch and calls `close`, which takes `self.window` and removes the window. Nothing guards this. The only check is `if let Some(w) = self.window.take()`, and the window exists after a manual show. The test `the_picture_can_be_turned_off...` only asserts `watched(...).2` right after `show()`. It never reports a second step, so it does not assert that the picture closes on the next step. Its "Shown on request all the same" comment shows the author intends on-request display to work. The settings text ("bring it back from the tray") is consistent with that intent. The picture closes on the agent's next step, usually within seconds, so the Show button does not keep it open. The effect is limited: a user who has turned the picture off gets a short flash and a dead button.

findings.title: API Keys page reports an environment-variable key as "Saved in Keychain" and offers a Remove that cannot remove it
findings.summary: `saved_keys` is seeded with `secrets::api_key(p.id).is_some()`, and that function checks the environment variable before the Keychain. A user with only OPENAI_API_KEY set sees "Saved in <credential store>" and a Remove button. The page's `from_env` branch ("Using $X from your shell") only shows after the user clicks Remove.
findings.failure_scenario: OPENAI_API_KEY is exported and nothing is in the Keychain. Settings > API Keys shows OpenAI as "Saved in Keychain" with "••••••••" and Remove. Clicking Remove calls `secrets::delete_api_key(id)`, whose failure is discarded with `let _`. The UI flips to "Using $OPENAI_API_KEY from your shell", while `api_providers.retain(...)` and `ws.direct_models.remove(id)` drop the provider's fetched model list from the running session. The key still works from the environment, so the user thinks they removed a key and did not, and the provider's models vanish until the next detect.
findings.evidence: settings_view.rs:332 `saved_keys.insert(p.id, secrets::api_key(p.id).is_some());`; trek-core/src/settings.rs:1103-1112 `api_key` returns `std::env::var(env)` first; pages.rs:636-640 `let from_env = ...; match (saved, from_env) { (true, _) => format!("Saved in {}", ...)`; pages.rs:652 `let _ = secrets::delete_api_key(id); this.saved_keys.insert(id, false);` then `ws.direct_models.remove(id)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Seed `saved_keys` from a Keychain-only read (not the env-first `api_key`). Only mark a key removed when `delete_api_key` succeeds, and show a toast on failure.

verdicts.reasoning: I read the quoted code in the working tree and the evidence is accurate. SettingsView::new seeds saved_keys with secrets::api_key(p.id).is_some() (settings_view.rs:332). trek_core secrets::api_key (settings.rs:1103) returns the env var value first and only then reads the Keychain. The only guard is the isolated() early return, which does not apply to a normal run. In pages.rs, status is matched on (saved, from_env), so with saved=true the "Saved in <store>" arm wins, and the Remove control shows because `if saved`. The "Using $X from your shell" arm only appears when saved=false, which only happens after Remove or when nothing is found. The Remove handler discards delete_api_key's result with `let _`, sets saved_keys to false, and removes the provider from api_providers and from ws.direct_models. For an env-only key the Keychain delete fails (no entry), but the key still resolves from the environment. The workspace detect pass (workspace.rs ~5640) fetches models for env-key providers, so direct_models was populated and is dropped until the next detect or fetch. One part of the reporter's scenario is slightly off: an env-only provider was never in api_providers, so the retain is a no-op. The mislabel, the useless Remove and the lost model list are real. Impact is moderate, not data loss: the models come back on the next detect. No test asserts this behaviour as intended.

I read the code on disk and every quoted line is present. SettingsView::new seeds saved_keys with secrets::api_key(p.id).is_some() (settings_view.rs:332). secrets::api_key (trek-core settings.rs:1103) returns the env var value first when it is non-empty, and only then falls back to the Keychain. With OPENAI_API_KEY exported and nothing in the Keychain, saved_keys[openai] is true. api_keys_page (pages.rs:635-640) matches (saved=true, _) and shows "Saved in <store>", plus the "••••••••" and Remove control. The Remove handler runs `let _ = secrets::delete_api_key(id)`. That function only deletes the Keychain entry, so it returns an error that is discarded. The handler then sets saved_keys to false, drops the provider from api_providers, and removes ws.direct_models[id]. The page then shows "Using $OPENAI_API_KEY from your shell" because the env var is still set. I found no test that asserts this behaviour. Two limits on the claim: the mislabel only appears when the env key is set, and I did not run the app. The path is reachable by reading, and the models disappear until the next fetch_direct_models. The reporter's "until the next detect" is roughly right, since fetch_direct_models is triggered from workspace.rs and the picker. Impact is a misleading status plus a lost provider model list, not data loss or a crash.

findings.title: A draft's first message is lost when the thread's folder or row can't be created
findings.summary: The composer clears its text and attachments before calling send_in; start_thread only puts them back for MakeThreadError::Worktree. A Folder error (new_chat_dir failed) or Create error (store refused the row) shows a toast and drops what the user typed.
findings.failure_scenario: Route::Draft { project: None }, the data folder is on a full disk or a volume that just went read-only (or `chats_dir()` can't be created). The user types a long prompt, attaches two screenshots and presses Return. composer.rs 418 `state.update(cx, |s, cx| s.set_value("", window, cx))` and 421 `std::mem::take(&mut self.outbox.paths)` empty the composer; send() -> start_thread -> make_thread -> `trek_core::paths::new_chat_dir().map_err(MakeThreadError::Folder)` fails; start_thread emits only the toast because `matches!(e, MakeThreadError::Worktree(_))` is false; the text and images are gone.
findings.evidence: workspace.rs 3151-3165: `Err(e) => { cx.emit(WorkspaceEvent::Toast { message: e.to_string(), undo: None }); // The message goes back to the composer when its worktree couldn't be planned. if matches!(e, MakeThreadError::Worktree(_)) { cx.emit(WorkspaceEvent::InsertIntoComposer(text.to_string())); for image in images { cx.emit(WorkspaceEvent::AttachImage(image.clone())); } } None }`. 3174-3177: `None => trek_core::paths::new_chat_dir().map_err(|e| MakeThreadError::Folder(e.to_string()))?`; 3189: `.map_err(|e| MakeThreadError::Create(e.to_string()))?`. composer.rs 418-421 clears the field and outbox before 442 `ws.send_in(&scope, text, images, cx)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the text and images for every MakeThreadError (drop the `matches!` guard), or have the composer keep its content until send_in reports success.

verdicts.reasoning: I read workspace.rs and composer.rs on disk. The composer clears the input at line 418 and takes the outbox paths at line 421 before it calls ws.send_in at line 442. send_in with Scope::Main calls send, and send for Route::Draft calls start_thread. start_thread restores the text and images (InsertIntoComposer, AttachImage) only when `matches!(e, MakeThreadError::Worktree(_))`. make_thread can also return Folder (new_chat_dir, which does create_dir_all) and Create (store.create_thread). Both of those only toast, and start_thread returns None, so send returns and the content is gone. No guard, retry or test covers this. The only other InsertIntoComposer emitters are the deep link and the browser panel. The Folder path needs a failing disk or a read-only data dir, which is rare. Create fails only if the store write fails. So the scenario is narrow, but the code path is real and the loss is unconditional once it is hit. The reporter's evidence is quoted accurately. The sub-case where the user typed a prompt before the failure is also real. There is one nuance: a Folder error only occurs when project is None (chat), but Create can occur for projects too.

I checked the code by reading. I did not run a repro or a test. The evidence is quoted accurately and the lines are not guarded. composer.rs send() clears the field (`set_value("")`) and takes the attachments (`std::mem::take(&mut self.outbox.paths)`) before it calls `ws.send_in(&scope, text, images, cx)`. In the non-edit branch it never gives them back, and it always returns `sent = true`. `send_in` with `Scope::Main` calls `send`. In `Route::Draft`, `send` calls `start_thread`, which calls `make_thread`. `make_thread` can return `MakeThreadError::Folder` when `new_chat_dir()` fails (it does `create_dir_all`, which fails on a full or read-only volume). It can also return `Create` when `store.create_thread` fails (a DB write error, or `ensure_project` failing for a project draft). `start_thread` emits the toast for every error, but only re-emits `InsertIntoComposer` and `AttachImage` when `matches!(e, MakeThreadError::Worktree(_))`. Folder and Create errors fall through to `None`, and `send` returns, so the text and images are not restored. The doc comment says the message goes back only when a worktree couldn't be planned. That is a deliberate narrow scope, not a statement that losing the message in the other cases is intended. I found no test that asserts the loss. The failure needs a disk or DB error, so it is rare. It is a genuine loss of user input, and the Worktree path already shows the intended behaviour is to restore it.

findings.title: Delegating from a no-project chat creates a sidebar project for ~/Trek/Chats/<timestamp>
findings.summary: `delegate` creates the sub-agent's thread with `create_thread(parent.cwd.as_deref(), …)`. For a parent started with no project, `parent.cwd` is its private chat folder (`~/Trek/Chats/<ts>`, git-inited by `new_chat_dir`), so `ensure_project` inserts a project row for that folder. `Project::is_workspace` returns true for it (it has a `.git`, and is not under /tmp, /private or the home junk list), so it is listed by `workspace_projects()` in the sidebar's project menu, the draft project picker and `list_threads`' "projects". `make_thread` and `handoff` deliberately avoid this (`(!chat).then_some(cwd)` and `project_dir` filtering `is_chat_dir`); `delegate` does not.
findings.failure_scenario: User starts a thread with no project (Route::Draft { project: None }) so its cwd is ~/Trek/Chats/2026-10-15-143012-123. The agent calls delegate_task. `create_thread(Some(chat_dir))` → `ensure_project` → `project_root` finds the chat dir's own `.git` and inserts a projects row with name "2026-10-15-143012-123". After the next `reload` (any new thread, handoff, or relaunch) the sidebar's "All projects" menu and the composer's project list show a project called "2026-10-15-143012-123" pointing at the chat folder; the sub-agent's `project_dir` is the chat dir instead of None. In tests the data dir is under /tmp or /private, so `is_workspace` hides it and no test sees it.
findings.evidence: orchestrate.rs:376 `let mut child = self.store.create_thread(parent.cwd.as_deref(), agent, model, effort, hand_holding)…`; orchestrate.rs:379 `child.cwd = parent.cwd.clone();` — contrast workspace.rs make_thread `self.store.create_thread((!chat).then_some(cwd.as_path()), …)` and lineage.rs:292-293 `let project = self.project_dir(&parent); … create_thread(project.as_deref(), …)` where worktrees.rs:22 `project_dir` filters `!trek_core::paths::is_chat_dir(c)`. trek-core store.rs:696 `let project = cwd.map(|p| self.ensure_project(p)).transpose()?;` store.rs:415-424 project_root_in returns the first ancestor with `.git` (the chat dir itself). paths.rs:80-91 chats_dir = `home().join("Trek").join("Chats")` in production, new_chat_dir runs `git init -q`. store.rs:73 `is_repo: path.join(".git").exists()`, store.rs:77-89 is_workspace → `self.is_repo` after the junk/tmp/private checks.
findings.suggested_fix: In `delegate`, pass the parent's project folder rather than its cwd: `let project = self.project_dir(&parent); self.store.create_thread(project.as_deref(), …)` (as `handoff` does), then keep `child.cwd = parent.cwd.clone()`. Optionally have `ensure_project`/`project_in` refuse paths under `chats_dir()` as a backstop.

verdicts.reasoning: Traced the path. make_thread for a no-project thread calls new_chat_dir (git-inited, under ~/Trek/Chats in production) and sets thread.cwd to it, while passing None to create_thread so no project is created. delegate passes parent.cwd.as_deref() to create_thread, which calls ensure_project -> project_in -> project_root(path). project_root returns the first ancestor with .git, which is the chat dir itself, so a projects row is inserted. Project::from_row sets is_repo from .git existing. is_workspace returns true: chat dir is not home, Downloads, Desktop or Documents, not under /tmp or /private, and is_repo is true. reload (workspace.rs:1624) loads store.projects(), and workspace_projects() has no is_chat_dir filter. It feeds the sidebar, composer, command palette and list_threads. handoff avoids this through project_dir, which filters is_chat_dir. delegate does not. I found no guard. The reporter's detail that the child's project_dir becomes the chat dir is a minor extra and not needed for the verdict.

I could not run the scenario, because the production chats_dir is under the real home and a test build would be slow. I traced it by reading the code instead. make_thread creates a no-project thread with new_chat_dir() (~/Trek/Chats/<ts>, git init'd). It calls create_thread(None, ...) so no project row is made, then sets thread.cwd to the chat dir. delegate (orchestrate.rs:376) calls create_thread(parent.cwd.as_deref(), ...) with that same chat dir as Some(path). create_thread then calls ensure_project, which calls project_in. project_in calls project_root, which returns the first ancestor with .git, and that is the chat dir itself. It INSERTs a projects row with name = the timestamp folder name, and nothing filters is_chat_dir on that path. self.projects = store.projects() (workspace.rs:1624) loads all rows. workspace_projects() filters only with is_workspace and hidden_projects. is_workspace excludes only the user-added list, home, Downloads, Desktop, Documents, /tmp, /private and Documents/Codex. ~/Trek/Chats/<ts> matches none of these and has .git, so is_repo is true and it is listed. The child's project_id is the chat project, which differs from the parent's None. I found no test asserting this behaviour. Tests use a data dir under /tmp or /private, which is_workspace hides, so none would catch it. The other creation sites (make_thread, handoff and lineage via project_dir) filter chat dirs, which shows the intent.

findings.title: split_words treats backslash as an escape, so a Windows path typed in the MCP add row (`node C:\srv\index.js`) loses its backslashes
findings.summary: McpServerConfig::parse and mcp::read_servers split a typed command line with split_words, which implements POSIX quoting: a backslash outside quotes drops itself and keeps the next character. On Windows paths are written with backslashes and no shell there treats them as escapes, so the command's path and any path argument are silently mangled before the server is saved.
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows the user types name `fs`, command `node C:\Users\me\mcp\index.js` into Settings > Tools > MCP add row (settings_view.rs:993 passes the text straight to read_servers). split_words yields ["node", "C:Usersmemcpindex.js"]. The server is saved and started as `node C:Usersmemcpindex.js`, which fails with 'Cannot find module'. The same happens for a `claude mcp add fs -- node C:\srv\index.js` line copied from docs. (A JSON paste survives only because JSON decoding restores the backslashes.)
findings.suggested_fix: Make backslash an escape only when not on Windows (cfg!(windows) → treat `\` as an ordinary character, matching PowerShell/cmd), or only when the following character is one of the shell's special characters (space, quote, backslash, $). Keep single/double-quote handling as is.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked the quoted code at crates/trek-core/src/mcp.rs:49-90. The evidence is accurate. Outside quotes, a backslash that is not at the start of a word before whitespace falls into the second `'\\'` arm. That arm drops the backslash and pushes the next char, so `C:\srv\index.js` becomes `C:srvindex.js`. Then I followed the callers. read_servers (mcp.rs:22) calls split_words, and for the plain-command case McpServerConfig::parse (settings.rs:379) calls it again and uses the mangled words as command and args. settings_view.rs add_mcp_server (~line 993) passes the raw text from the add row into read_servers with no platform handling. Windows is a shipped target: .github/workflows/release-windows.yml exists, along with trek-ipc/src/windows.rs, trek-mcp/src/desktop/windows.rs and many cfg(windows) blocks. I found no Windows-specific branch in split_words, parse or read_servers. The only tests (mcp.rs:402-408) assert POSIX behaviour (`c\ d` becomes `c d`, line continuations). None covers a Windows path, so nothing marks the mangling as intended. The JSON route (from_json_text) is unaffected, as the reporter said. Their other claim, the `"command": "uvx x"` string-splitting path (mcp.rs:250), only splits when the string contains a space and the path does not exist, so a Windows path with spaces in that JSON field would also be mangled. Quoting the path ('C:\x' or "C:\x") avoids the problem, which limits severity. It is still a silent mangling that gives a confusing 'Cannot find module' error.

I read mcp.rs and settings.rs on disk. The quoted code is accurate. split_words has no platform branch, and read_servers and McpServerConfig::parse both call it. settings_view.rs:993 passes the typed text straight to read_servers. Windows is a shipped target: the repo has release-windows.yml and Windows-specific crates and deps. I copied the exact split_words body into a scratch program under /tmp and ran it on the reported inputs. It mangled both. The existing tests only cover POSIX quoting. They do not assert that dropping Windows backslashes is intended. quote() single-quotes any word containing a backslash, so a path that was already saved survives a round trip. The loss happens only on first entry of an unquoted Windows path. The user can work around it by quoting the path in single quotes or using forward slashes, so this is medium or low severity.

findings.title: Photo uploads are rendered at screen scale (3x), making multi-megabyte uploads that can exceed the Mac's 8 MiB frame limit and drop the connection, losing the message
findings.summary: `PickedPhoto.upload` resizes to a 1600-point long side with `UIGraphicsImageRenderer(size:)`, whose default format uses the main screen scale, so the bitmap is 4800 px on the long side (17 MP), ~9x the pixels the comment promises. The quality loop stops at q≈0.34 regardless of size, so one photo is typically 1.5–3.5 MB after base64 (the Mac expects "about a megabyte"), and three or four photos in one `send` exceed the Mac's 8 MiB `max_message`, which closes the WebSocket. The composer has already cleared the text and photos by then.
findings.failure_scenario: User attaches 4 camera photos (PhotosPicker allows up to 4) and taps send. Composer builds 4 uploads of ~2–3 MB each (4800×3600 JPEG at q 0.34, base64), `model.send` writes one ~10 MB text frame, then ThreadView clears `composer.draft`/`composer.photos`. tungstenite rejects the oversized frame; server.rs's read loop returns on `Some(Err(_))`, closing the socket. TrekClient.receive throws → dropped() → AppModel.failPending fires the pending reply with "The connection to your Mac dropped…" as a toast. The message and photos are gone from the composer and never reach the agent; the phone reconnects and the same happens on retry.
findings.evidence: ios/Trek/Model/Photos.swift:5-6 comment "the long side at most 1600 points, under about 900 KB"; :15-18 `let scale = min(1, 1600 / max(longest, 1)) … UIGraphicsImageRenderer(size: size).image { … }` (no `UIGraphicsImageRendererFormat` with `scale = 1`, unlike ios/Trek/Demo/DemoParity.swift:34 and DemoNoteImages.swift:32 which set `format.scale = 1`); :21-24 loop `while let d = data, d.count > 900_000, quality > 0.35` returns whatever the last encode produced. ios/Trek/Views/Composer.swift:25 and NewThreadSheet.swift:114 `maxSelectionCount: 4`. ios/Trek/Views/ThreadView.swift:645-654 `let uploads = composer.photos.compactMap(\.upload) … model.send(…) ; composer.draft = ""; composer.photos = []`. crates/trek-remote/src/server.rs:98-99 `// Photos come base64 in send: a few of a megabyte each. max_message: 8 << 20`, :536-537 `.max_message_size/.max_frame_size`, :1225 `None | Some(Err(_)) | Some(Ok(Message::Close(_))) => return`. ios/Trek/Net/TrekClient.swift:293-296 receive error → `dropped(error)`; ios/Trek/Model/AppModel.swift:400-403 `failPending`.
findings.suggested_fix: Render with a `UIGraphicsImageRendererFormat` whose `scale = 1` (as the demo code does), and cap the per-message total (or reduce dimensions further) when the loop cannot get under the byte budget.

verdicts.reasoning: I read Photos.swift, ThreadView.send and the server's ws config. The quoted code is accurate. `UIGraphicsImageRenderer(size:)` is created with no format, so it uses the default format, whose scale is the main screen scale (3x on Pro iPhones). `UIImage(data:)` gives scale 1, so `image.size` is in pixels. A 4032x3024 camera photo becomes size 1600x1200 points, which renders as 4800x3600 px (17 MP). That is an upscale of the original. The `jpegData` call then encodes all of those pixels. The quality loop runs 0.82, 0.70, 0.58, 0.46, 0.34 and stops at 0.34 whatever the size, so the "under about 900 KB" comment does not hold. The other renderers in the repo (DemoParity, DemoNoteImages) set `format.scale = 1`, which confirms the intent. ThreadView.send builds the uploads, calls `model.send`, then clears `composer.draft` and `composer.photos` straight away. There is no retry or re-queue. The server sets `max_message_size` and `max_frame_size` to 8 MiB, and on a capacity error `ws.next()` yields `Err`, so the read loop returns and the connection closes. Up to 4 photos can be attached. Uncertainty: I did not measure the encoded size. A 17 MP JPEG at q 0.34 is roughly 1.2-3 MB depending on the scene. After base64 (x1.33), 4 detailed photos, or 3 busy ones, plausibly exceed 8.39 MB. Light scenes or 1-2 photos would pass. The scale bug and the broken size cap are certain. Hitting the 8 MiB limit depends on the photos, but it is realistic for multi-photo sends. Impact is a lost message and photos, with a toast. It is not a crash.

I checked the quoted code on disk. Photos.swift line 18 does use UIGraphicsImageRenderer(size:) without a scale-1 format. On a 3x iPhone the bitmap is therefore 4800 px on the long side, and the quality loop ends at q≈0.34. So the first half of the claim holds. The send path has no size guard. The server caps messages at 8 MiB, and the client's 16 MiB limit only applies to frames it receives.

The size claim is wrong, though. To measure it I wrote a Swift/ImageIO program that follows the same pipeline: decode, draw at 3x of the 1600 px size, then the same quality loop (0.82 down to 0.34). I ran it on about 49 real HEIC/JPEG photos from this Mac, including nine iPhone HEICs.

Base64 size per photo was 0.9 to 2.2 MB, with a mean of about 1.7 MB. The reporter said 1.5 to 3.5 MB, and typical photos came out below that range. Four typical photos total about 6.7 MB, under the 8.39 MB limit. Even the four largest of the nine iPhone HEICs total only about 8.1 MB, which is also under it.

The connection drop would need four unusually detailed or noisy photos, such as night shots, to all land near the top of the range. I could not show that case. The reporter's "three or four photos typically exceed" does not hold.

The oversized-pixel bug is real, but it is a latent risk, not a demonstrated message-loss bug. This is only an approximation of UIKit's encoder, which could differ somewhat from the ImageIO output I measured.

1. Read ios/Trek/Model/Photos.swift. Line 18 calls `UIGraphicsImageRenderer(size:)` with no format, so it uses the default format at main-screen scale (3x on current iPhones). A 4032x3024 photo is sized to 1600x1200 points and rendered at 4800x3600 px. That is 9x the pixels meant, and more than the 4032 px original. The repo knows the pitfall: DemoParity.swift and DemoNoteImages.swift set `format.scale = 1`. The quality loop stops at q=0.34 whatever the size.

2. Traced the send path. ThreadView.send() builds uploads, calls model.send, then clears composer.draft and composer.photos without waiting for a reply. TrekClient.send encodes with JSONSerialization without .withoutEscapingSlashes, so every '/' in the base64 becomes '\/' (about +1.6%). The client's maximumMessageSize of 16 MiB only applies to receiving. On the Mac, ServerConfig::new sets max_message = 8 << 20, and trek-app/src/remote.rs:454 does not override it. serve() applies that limit as max_message_size and max_frame_size, and session_loop returns on Some(Err(_)), closing the socket. crates/trek-remote/tests/server.rs `oversized_messages_are_refused` confirms an oversized message closes the connection. The phone then hits dropped() and failPending(), shows the "connection dropped" toast, and the cleared text and photos are not restored. No test says the phone should send frames over 8 MiB.

3. Measured sizes in /tmp with a Swift/ImageIO copy of the exact resize and quality loop (3x scale, 0.82 down to 0.34 while over 900 KB, base64, JSONSerialization with sortedKeys):
- 20 real images (12MP iPhone HEICs and other photos) came to 0.88 to 2.21 MB of base64 each. The comment promises under about 900 KB. At 1x they would be 0.5 to 1.0 MB.
- The busiest four real photos in one `send` made a frame of 8,371,289 bytes against a limit of 8,388,608. That is 99.8%, so the reporter's "2-3 MB each, ~10 MB" is overstated for 12MP sources.
- Encoding those photos at native resolution (no upscaling) gives 0.64 to 0.82 bits per pixel at q 0.34. Applied to 4800x3600, that projects 1.84 to 2.36 MB base64 each, so about 8.6 to 8.8 MB for four, over the limit. Native-resolution detail is what a 24MP source (the default on iPhone 15 and later) would carry once scaled down to 4800 px.
So the overflow is not reproduced with 12MP photos (they stop just short) but is likely with busy 24MP photos. The 3x render is the cause: at scale 1 the same four total about 3 MB.

Nothing in the code guards against it: no total-size check on the phone and no chunking. Once triggered it fails the same way on every retry.

findings.title: Settings General and Project pages call `ready_agents()` in render, which does a Keychain lookup for every cloud provider on every frame
findings.summary: `general_page` and `project_page` call `Workspace::ready_agents()` from `render`. That function calls `secrets::api_key(p.id)` for each of the 8 non-local DIRECT_PROVIDERS, and that is a synchronous OS Keychain read when no env var is set. The settings page re-renders on every workspace notify.
findings.failure_scenario: The user opens Settings > General (or Project) while an agent streams. Each workspace notify re-renders the page, and each render issues 8 `keyring::Entry::get_password()` calls on the main thread. The Keychain can be slow or locked, and the lookups block the UI. The file's own `Probe` doc comment says "Never read from `render`", and the file otherwise follows it. The same pattern is why Settings pickers that depend on model lists can stutter.
findings.evidence: pages.rs:138 `let agents = ws.ready_agents();` (general_page) and :1369 (project_page); workspace.rs:3103-3105 `for p in catalog::DIRECT_PROVIDERS { if !p.local && trek_core::settings::secrets::api_key(p.id).is_some() {`; settings.rs:1103-1112 `api_key` ends in `keyring::Entry::new(SERVICE, provider).ok()?.get_password().ok()`.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache key presence (refresh it on save and remove of a key and on detect), or probe it off-thread as `SettingsView::probe` does, so `ready_agents` does no OS call.

verdicts.reasoning: I read the code at each hop and found no guard or cache. pages.rs:138 (general_page) and :1369 (project_page) call ws.ready_agents() directly while building the page. ready_agents (workspace.rs:3084) loops over catalog::DIRECT_PROVIDERS and, for every non-local provider, calls trek_core::settings::secrets::api_key(p.id). api_key returns early only when paths::isolated() is true, which is the test and verify mode. Otherwise it returns the env var if one is set and non-empty. If there is no env var, it falls through to keyring::Entry::new(..).get_password(), a synchronous macOS Keychain call. Nothing caches the result. The only static in that module is the in-memory MCP map used for isolated mode. settings_view.rs:132, 334 and 355 observe the workspace and call cx.notify(), so the open Settings window re-renders on every workspace notify. I did not run the app or measure Keychain latency. The reporter is right about the mechanism, but the user-visible cost is unmeasured. A normal unlocked lookup is probably sub-millisecond to a few ms, so the likely effect is small jank rather than a freeze. The Keychain-locked or slow case is plausible but speculative. The problem is also not specific to Settings. ready_agents is called from other render paths too, including composer.rs:1366 and composer/pickers.rs:352, so the real defect is in ready_agents itself. The reporter's "Probe doc says never read from render" point is a style argument. That doc comment at settings_view.rs:246 is about the Probe type, not about this call.

I checked the quoted code and it matches the working tree. general_page (pages.rs:138) and project_page (pages.rs:1369) are called from SettingsView render (settings_view.rs:1403-1404). SettingsView observes the workspace and calls cx.notify() on every workspace notify (settings_view.rs:132, 334). Workspace::ready_agents (workspace.rs:3084) loops over DIRECT_PROVIDERS and calls secrets::api_key(p.id) for each non-local provider. api_key only returns early when the process is isolated or the provider's env var is set. Otherwise it calls keyring::Entry::get_password(), a synchronous Keychain read. Nothing caches the result. The Probe doc comment in settings_view.rs:246 says "Never read from render", and SettingsView::new reads the keys once into saved_keys, so the claim that this page breaks the file's own rule holds. I found no test that asserts the behaviour is intended. I measured it with a scratch Swift program in /tmp that did 8 SecItemCopyMatching lookups for missing generic-password items. It took about 6-8 ms per batch on this machine, so each render of those pages costs roughly half a frame on the main thread when no env keys are set. That is a real but modest cost, and it grows if the Keychain is locked or slow. Two points weaken the claim. First, the reporter's "UI blocks" scenario is mostly speculation: 8 misses cost only a few ms. Second, the same pattern already runs from other render paths (sidebar.rs:1329 via usage_providers, and composer pickers), so Settings is not unique.

findings.title: TeX parser recurses without a depth limit on `\text{{{…` and chained argument commands; a ~20 KB formula overflows the main-thread stack
findings.summary: MathParse.maxDepth (48) is only enforced in `list()` and `textArg()`. `textInner` recurses into itself directly on every `{`, and `arg()` → `atom()` → `command()` → `arg()` (for \frac, \sqrt, \hat, \boxed, \mathbb, …) never touches `depth` either. MathRender.image only caps the formula at 20,000 characters, so an agent answer can drive thousands of nested frames on the main thread (iOS main-thread stack is 1 MB).
findings.failure_scenario: An assistant message contains `$$\text{` followed by ~19,000 `{` characters (or `$$` + `\frac` × 4,000 + `$$`). MathDetect.splitDisplay yields a closed display region; MarkdownText → MathBlock → MathRender.image(tex, display: true) passes the 20,000-char check and calls MathParse.parse on the main thread inside SwiftUI body evaluation. textInner (or arg/atom/command) recurses ~19,000 (or ~4,000 × 3) frames deep, each with array/string locals, exceeding the 1 MB main-thread stack: the app crashes with EXC_BAD_ACCESS the moment the thread is opened, and again on every relaunch that reopens it (the transcript is cached).
findings.evidence: ios/Trek/Views/Math/MathParse.swift:9 `static let maxDepth = 48`; :268-270 depth is incremented/checked only in `list(_:)`; :460-462 only in `textArg`; :465-481 `mutating func textInner … case "{": flush(); out.append(contentsOf: textInner(face))` (direct recursion, no depth change); :367-376 `arg()` → `default: return atom()`; :379-389 `atom()` → `case "\\": … return command(name)`; :561-564 `case "frac", …: let num = arg(); let den = arg()`. ios/Trek/Views/Math/MathText.swift:43 `let nodes = tex.count <= 20_000 ? MathParse.parse(tex) : nil` is the only size guard; MathText.swift:306-311 and :339-341 call it from view bodies. MathDetect.swift:96/220 limit only inline (`$…$`) formulas to 2000 bytes; display formulas are unbounded.
findings.suggested_fix: Increment and check `depth` in `textInner` (on `{`), `arg()` and `atom()` (or in `command()`), falling back to `restAsText()`/`.unknown` past maxDepth; alternatively run MathParse/MathLayout off the main thread with a larger stack, as the formula image is cached anyway.

verdicts.reasoning:
I read the parser, the size guard and the view call sites, and traced both recursion paths.

1. `maxDepth = 48` is applied in only two places: `list()` (lines 268-270) and `textArg()` (lines 460-462). `arg()` and `atom()` have no depth handling.
2. `textInner` handles `{` with `out.append(contentsOf: textInner(face))`. That is direct self-recursion with no depth change, so `textArg`'s check runs once at the top and never again.
3. `\text{` reaches this path: `command("text")` returns `.group(textArg(.main))`. About 19,000 `{` characters after it produce about 19,000 nested `textInner` frames.
4. The `\frac` chain is a second path. `command("frac")` calls `arg()`. For a non-brace, non-nil token `arg()` calls `atom()`, `atom()` consumes `\` and calls `command()`, and `command("frac")` calls `arg()` again. `list()` is never entered, so `depth` stays 0 and the depth cap does not apply. A chain of `\frac\frac…` is therefore unbounded, with about 3 frames per level. `command()` is a very large switch, so its frames are probably large.
5. Reachability holds. `MathText.swift:43` only caps the formula at 20,000 characters. `MathDetect.closing` applies `inlineMax` only when `inline` is true, so `$$…$$` display regions are unbounded. `MarkdownText` case `.math` renders `MathBlock`, and `MathBlock.body` calls `MathRender.image(tex, display: true, …)` synchronously, so `MathParse.parse` runs on the main thread during view body evaluation.
6. I found no iOS tests that cover depth or nesting. No test asserts this behaviour as intended.
7. The overflow depends on frame size, which I did not measure. At 19,000 frames a `textInner` frame only needs to exceed about 55 bytes to pass 1 MB. That frame holds an array, a string, a closure context and a scalar, so it is almost certainly larger. The `\frac` path has even bigger frames.
8. Severity is medium because it needs a crafted or prompt-injected assistant message. The result is a crash on open and again on relaunch if the transcript is cached. I did not verify the caching claim.

Read the code and confirmed textInner recurses on every `{` with no depth change. Only list() and textArg() check depth, and arg()->atom()->command()->arg() never touches it. MathRender.image only checks tex.count <= 20_000, and MathBlock calls it from body. Then I built a standalone driver that compiles the real MathParse.swift and MathTables.swift. It runs MathParse.parse on a Foundation Thread with a 1 MB stack, which is the iOS main-thread size. Small inputs parse fine. The inputs from the claim, `\text{` plus 19000 `{` and `\frac` x 4000, die with exit 138 (SIGBUS, stack overflow) in both release and debug builds. In release, `\text{{{` crashes between 2000 and 5000 braces. `\frac` x 1000 parses in release but crashes in debug, and `\frac` x 4000 crashes in both. Both sizes are well under the 20,000-character guard. I did not trace MarkdownText's display-math path to its end, but MathBlock is called from MarkdownText.swift:59 and MathDetect only limits inline formulas (inlineMax = 2000), so display formulas are unbounded. I did not run the real iOS app. The 1 MB limit comes from the driver thread, not from a device.

findings.title: Switching agent mid-turn leaves the interrupted prompt held, and the next session sends it
findings.summary: set_prefs_in's agent switch closes the running turn, pushes 'Interrupted' and shuts the old session down, but does not clear live.held. A prompt still waiting behind its checkpoint job stays there and is dispatched to the new agent's session by run_git once that session attaches, together with the user's next message.
findings.failure_scenario: Thread in a git repo. User sends A: send_as queues GitJob::Checkpoint (3361) and dispatch() holds Command::Prompt{A} (4545-4546) while the snapshot runs (seconds on a big repo). Before it finishes the user picks another agent in the composer: set_prefs_in takes turn_started, close_turn, pushes 'Interrupted' (2745-2751), sends Shutdown and sets commands=None (2777-2778); live.held still holds A. git_done -> run_git: no jobs, commands None, held stays (4571). User sends B: send_as -> ensure_session -> attach -> run_git runs B's checkpoint; dispatch holds B too; when the checkpoint lands run_git sends held = [A, B] (4572-4575) to the new agent, which works on the prompt the transcript shows as interrupted and then on B. interrupt() (4470-4473), archive (5086) and end_task_now (orchestrate.rs 791) all clear held in the same situation; set_prefs_in does not.
findings.evidence: workspace.rs 2741-2752: `if switched { live.billing = None; live.permissions.clear(); live.picks.clear(); if live.turn_started.take().is_some() { live.close_turn(false); ... live.items.push(Item::Notice { text: "Interrupted".into() }); ... } }` -- no `live.held` handling. 2776-2781: `if before.agent != prefs.agent || relaunch { let _ = tx.try_send(Command::Shutdown); live.commands = None; live._events = None; ... }`. 4568-4580: `let Some(job) = live.git_jobs.pop_front() else { let Some(tx) = &live.commands else { return }; let held = std::mem::take(&mut live.held); ... for cmd in held { let _ = tx.try_send(cmd); } ... }`. 3521: attach() ends with `self.run_git(&thread, cx)`. Contrast 4470-4471: `if live.held.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Command::Prompt { .. })) { live.held.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Command::Prompt { .. })); ...`.
findings.suggested_fix: When the switch cuts a running turn, drop held prompts as interrupt() does (`live.held.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Command::Prompt { .. }))`) before the 'Interrupted' notice.

verdicts.reasoning: I traced the scenario against the working tree. send_to_inner (about 3361) pushes GitJob::Checkpoint and then calls dispatch, which pushes Command::Prompt onto live.held whenever git_busy or git_jobs is non-empty (4549-4553). In set_prefs_in, the switched branch takes turn_started, closes the turn and pushes the "Interrupted" notice. The later `before.agent != prefs.agent` branch sends Shutdown and sets commands=None. Neither branch touches live.held, and no other statement in set_prefs_in does either. When git_done calls run_git, there are no jobs and commands is None, so it returns with held intact (4577-4578). The next send calls ensure_session, which calls attach (3528), which calls run_git. B's Checkpoint job is queued, and dispatch pushes B onto held. After the checkpoint lands, run_git flushes held = [A, B] to the new agent's tx. interrupt() (4477-4478), the archive path (5093) and orchestrate.rs:812 all clear held in the same situation, which shows clearing it is the intended behaviour. No test asserts that held survives an agent switch; my grep found none. The comment at 4577 says held is kept for a session that ended under it, but that is meant for a prompt the user still wants sent. Here the transcript marks the prompt as Interrupted. One extra route: send_queued (3415) calls ensure_session when commands is None and held contains a Prompt. That can start the new agent's session with A even before the user sends B. The impact is narrow: it needs a git repo, an agent switch during the checkpoint window, and a slow snapshot.

I read the current working-tree code and did not run a test. I confirmed each step of the scenario in order.

1. send_as, when a turn is not already running, sets turn_started, pushes GitJob::Checkpoint if the thread is in a repo, then calls dispatch(Command::Prompt). dispatch pushes the prompt onto live.held while git_busy is set or git_jobs is non-empty. So a prompt is held while the checkpoint runs.

2. set_prefs_in, on an agent switch, takes turn_started, calls close_turn(false) and pushes the "Interrupted" notice. It then sends Shutdown, sets commands=None and drops _events. It never touches live.held. close_turn only touches tasks and tool rows.

3. When the checkpoint finishes, git_done calls run_git. With no jobs left and commands None, run_git returns early and leaves held as it is. The code comment says this is deliberate: "what's held stays held, for the session that starts next (attach)".

4. When the user sends B, ensure_session creates the new agent's session. attach ends with run_git, which runs B's checkpoint. When that finishes, run_git does mem::take(held) and sends every held command to the new agent. That is [A, B]. The same applies if send_queued calls ensure_session first (3415 checks for a Prompt in held while commands is None).

5. Nothing else clears held in this situation. interrupt() (4477-4478), archive (5093) and end_task_now (orchestrate.rs 812) all do clear it. The one test that covers a mid-turn switch, switching_agent_leaves_nothing_waiting_on_the_old_one, never sets up a held prompt, so it does not assert the behaviour is intended.

Limits on the impact: the window is the length of the checkpoint snapshot, so this only happens when the user switches agent during that time. When it does, the new agent gets a prompt the transcript shows as interrupted, ahead of B. That is wrong behaviour against the code's own intent: the switch is meant to leave nothing waiting on the old agent, and an interrupted turn should not run. I rate it low to medium.

findings.title: show_in_main with a thread or draft while the main window is in Editor mode lands nowhere visible
findings.summary: navigate only drops back to Agents mode for Settings/Basecamp/Notes/Onboarding. A thread window's fork (Scope::Thread) and its ⌘N call show_in_main(Route::Thread/Draft): the harness route changes behind the editor, ActivateMain brings the editor forward, and the fork's message is composed into the hidden harness composer.
findings.failure_scenario: Main window in Editor mode (⌥⌘E). The user forks from a thread window (fork_thread with scope Scope::Thread): 4910 `self.show_in_main(Route::Thread(fork_id.clone()), cx)` -> navigate leaves mode == Editor; 4915-4916 emits ComposeIn { scope: Scope::Main, thread: fork } which root.rs 242-245 accepts because thread_id_in(&Scope::Main) is the new route, so the message goes into the harness composer that isn't drawn; the main window comes forward showing the editor with its previous chat. Likewise ⌘N in a thread window (thread_window.rs 246-249) changes the invisible harness route to a draft and FocusComposer is swallowed by root.rs 176 (`... if this.workspace.read(cx).ide() => {}`). reveal_now (root.rs 974) uses open_thread_here for exactly this case; show_in_main does not.
findings.evidence: workspace.rs 1789-1792: `pub fn show_in_main(&mut self, route: Route, cx: &mut Context<Self>) { self.navigate(route, cx); cx.emit(WorkspaceEvent::ActivateMain); }`. 2152-2154: `if self.ide() && matches!(route, Route::Settings(_) | Route::Basecamp | Route::Notes | Route::Onboarding) { self.mode = Mode::Agents; }`. 4907-4916: `let into = if *scope == Scope::Ide { Scope::Ide } else { Scope::Main }; match scope { ... Scope::Thread(_) => self.show_in_main(Route::Thread(fork_id.clone()), cx), ... } if let Some((text, images)) = message { if self.main_window.is_some() { cx.emit(WorkspaceEvent::ComposeIn { scope: into, thread: fork_id.clone(), text, images, edit: None }); }`. thread_window.rs 246-249: `.on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &NewThread, _, cx| { this.show_in_main(Route::Draft { project: None }, cx) }))`. root.rs 176: `WorkspaceEvent::FocusComposer | ... if this.workspace.read(cx).ide() => {}`. ide.rs 268-270 open_thread_here handles the editor case.
findings.suggested_fix: In show_in_main, route Thread/Draft through open_thread_here / ide_new_chat when ide() (and target ComposeIn at Scope::Ide), or switch to Mode::Agents before navigating.

verdicts.reasoning: I traced the path in the working tree. show_in_main (workspace.rs 1796) calls navigate and then emits ActivateMain. navigate (about line 2152) only sets mode = Agents for Settings, Basecamp, Notes and Onboarding. For Route::Thread and Route::Draft in Editor mode, the harness route changes behind the editor and mode stays Editor. ActivateMain calls show_main, which only activates the window. It does not change mode. fork_thread (4917) calls show_in_main for Scope::Thread. It then emits ComposeIn { scope: Main }. root.rs accepts that event because thread_id_in(Main) is now the fork, so the message goes to the hidden harness composer. FocusComposer is dropped in root.rs 176 when ide() is true. reveal_now in root.rs handles the Editor case with open_thread_here, which opens the thread in the AI side bar. show_in_main has no such handling. The same defect also affects other show_in_main callers: lineage::go with from_window, background_use::open_thread, worktrees.rs 327, and the thread window's NewThread action. A search of the tests directory found no test for show_in_main in Editor mode, so nothing marks this as intended. One part of the report is overstated: nothing is lost. The fork and its composed message sit in the harness and appear after the user toggles back to Agents mode. The bug is a UI action that visibly does nothing in the editor, not data loss.

I read the code on disk; the line numbers have drifted but the quoted code is all there. I did not run a test or a repro. show_in_main (workspace.rs ~1796) calls navigate and then emits ActivateMain. navigate only resets mode to Agents for Settings, Basecamp, Notes and Onboarding. For Route::Thread and Route::Draft it leaves mode as Editor, so only the hidden harness route changes. Nothing else reconciles this. root.rs:815 maps ActivateMain to show_main, which only activates the window. root.rs:176 drops FocusComposer, InsertIntoComposer and AttachImage while ide() is true. open_thread_here (ide.rs:268) does branch on ide(), but show_in_main does not use it. Callers confirm the path is reachable. fork_thread's Scope::Thread arm calls show_in_main(Route::Thread(fork)). The ThreadWindow NewThread action calls show_in_main(Draft). lineage::go with from_window=true and background_use::open_thread also call it. In fork_thread, ComposeIn{scope: Main} is then accepted by root.rs because thread_id_in(Main) is the new route, so the text goes to the harness composer, which is not drawn. Settings routes are special-cased in navigate, which shows the authors meant a thread-window action to be visible in the main window. No test covers show_in_main with ide() true. The impact is limited: nothing is lost, and switching back to Agents mode (via mode toggle or ⌥⌘E) shows the thread or draft. I corrected the reporter on two points. FocusComposer is emitted by navigate, not by NewThread itself. The mode-switch back to Agents can also navigate to the active IDE chat when follow_active_chat is on, so the composed fork may not be shown right away. That does not change the core defect.

findings.title: Picker stays open after the caret moves; Enter then replaces the text between the caret and the stale trigger
findings.summary: The @/$// trigger is recomputed only on InputEvent::Change (composer.rs:222 -> pickers::update_trigger), never on caret movement, and the textarea emits no selection event. So after a click, Home, or arrow-left the picker remains open with the old `Trigger { start }`, and accept_pick selects `t.start..cursor` using the *new* caret, replacing arbitrary message text with the pick.
findings.failure_scenario: Type "fix the bug in @main" (picker opens, trigger.start = 15). Click on the word "bug" (caret = 8); the picker is still showing. Press Enter (picker_key: n > 0 -> accept_pick). set_selected_range(15..8) becomes the reversed selection 8..15 ("bug in "), and replace() writes "@src/main.rs " over it: the message is now "fix the @src/main.rs @main". Pressing Home before Enter wipes everything before the `@`. The same happens with mouse clicks on a picker row after the caret moved.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run update_trigger whenever the caret moves (observe the input state and compare cursor to the stored trigger range), or in accept_pick bail out unless `t.start < cursor && cursor <= t.start + 1 + t.query.len()` and the text at t.start is still the trigger character; also close the picker when the caret leaves the token.

verdicts.reasoning: I traced the path from the composer subscription to accept_pick. The trigger is recomputed only in the composer's InputEvent::Change handler, in insert_trigger, and at the end of accept_pick. Change is emitted only on text edits and undo/redo replay (state.rs lines 2895, 3853 and 4180). Caret movement by click, Home or arrow keys emits no event. The only observer on the input just calls cx.notify(). The picker's own key handler (picker_action) takes only up, down, escape, tab and enter, so Left and Home go straight to the textarea. Nothing re-validates the stale trigger against the cursor. In accept_pick, `s.cursor()` is read at accept time and `set_selected_range(t.start..cursor)` is called with the stale t.start. When cursor < start, `move_to(start)` followed by `select_to(cursor)` goes through extend_selection, which swaps the ends instead of rejecting the range. replace() then overwrites cursor..start with the pick. The failure scenario therefore holds: Enter with the picker open and the caret moved to before the trigger replaces the text between them. I did not run it and found no test asserting the behaviour. One small correction: the picker rows still come from the old query "main", which matches the reporter's picture.

I read the code and did not run it. I could not build a standalone repro. I checked five links in the chain, and each one holds.

1. The only place the composer refreshes the trigger is the `InputEvent::Change` branch (composer.rs:222-223). `pickers::update_trigger` is otherwise called only from `insert_trigger` and `accept_pick`. The ide/ai input does the same at input.rs:126.
2. Caret movement does not emit `Change`. `set_selected_range`, `move_to` and `select_to` in vendor/gpui-base state.rs emit nothing. The only emitters are `PressEnter`, `Focus`, `Blur` and the text-edit paths (lines 2895, 3853, 4180). The composer's `cx.observe(&input)` only calls `cx.notify()` and does not touch the trigger.
3. Nothing else closes the picker. `picker_key` handles only escape, up, down, enter and tab, and every other key falls through to the textarea, so left and Home move the caret without clearing it. There is no blur, click-outside or caret handler for the picker in composer.rs, pickers.rs or ide/ai/input.rs.
4. `accept_pick` clones the stale `t`, reads the new `s.cursor()` and calls `set_selected_range(t.start..cursor)`. That calls `move_to(15)` and then `select_to(8)`, which gives a reversed selection covering 8..15. `replace` then calls `replace_text_in_range_silent(None, ...)`, which replaces the active selection, so text between the caret and the old `@` is overwritten.
5. Neither the tests nor the code treat this as intended behaviour. I found no test covering caret movement while a picker is open.

The scenario holds as stated for a click or arrow-left to a point before the trigger. The click-on-the-row variant also holds, because the row's `on_click` calls `accept_pick` with the same stale trigger. If the caret moves after the trigger start, the range is only shortened. That case is benign for the span between the `@` and the caret, but it still leaves the rest of the query text in place.

One small correction: the final text in the reporter's example may differ slightly by spacing, but the corruption itself is real.

findings.title: file URIs are built for POSIX paths only, so LSP is unusable on Windows
findings.summary: uri_of percent-encodes every byte outside [A-Za-z0-9-._~/] after a bare `file://` prefix. A Windows path such as `C:\Users\me\a.rs` therefore becomes `file://C%3A%5CUsers%5Cme%5Ca.rs`: the drive and path end up in the host part, with no `file:///C:/...` form. path_of_uri has the same POSIX assumption.
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows, `rootUri` in `initialize_params` and the `didOpen` uri are both malformed. rust-analyzer or gopls cannot map the document to a file, so hover, completion and go-to-definition fail. Diagnostics published as `file:///C:/Users/...` also never equal the editor's `uri` string, because the watcher does `if u != uri { continue }`. The Problems panel and gutter stay empty. The module has cfg(windows) test paths, so Windows support is intended.
findings.evidence: lsp_client.rs:37-48: `let mut s = String::from("file://"); for b in path.to_str()?.bytes() { if UNRESERVED.contains(&b) { s.push(b as char); } else { s.push_str(&format!("%{b:02X}")); } }` with UNRESERVED = letters, digits, `-._~/` only (`:` and `\\` are encoded). editor.rs:~334 `if u != uri { continue; }`.

verdicts.reasoning: I read uri_of, path_of_uri and their callers. uri_of (lsp_client.rs:37) is the only URI builder and has no cfg(windows) branch. uri_for (line 691) wraps it and editor.rs:320 calls it. initialize_params (line 568) uses it for rootUri. findings.title: current_target() has no Windows arm, so registry agents that ship a Windows binary show 'Not for this PC' and cannot be installed on Windows

findings.failure_scenario: Windows user opens Settings > Agents > Add agent, searches Devin (binary-only distribution with windows-x86_64 in the registry). add_agent.rs:148 calls registry::plan(a, registry::current_target()) → current_target() is None → plan() returns None → the row reads 'Not for this PC' with no Add button. Nothing the user does can install it, although the macOS build of Trek installs the same entry from the same registry.

crates/trek-core/src/registry.rs:670: `let plan = plan(agent, current_target()).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("{} has no build for {}.", agent.name, if cfg!(windows) { "this PC" } else { "this Mac" }))?;`
crates/trek-core/fixtures/acp-registry.json:38 `"windows-x86_64": {`
crates/trek-app/src/add_agent.rs:148: `if registry::plan(a, registry::current_target()).is_none() { RowState::Unavailable } else { RowState::Available }`

The registry fixture has windows-x86_64 and windows-aarch64 binary targets. No test asserts this, and the code has Windows-specific handling for archives, the .exe suffix and backslash paths. Agents that also ship npx or uvx (kilo) still install on Windows through the npx fallback. The impact is therefore limited to binary-only agents.

findings.title: Typing while a thread's history loads starts its session from an empty recap
findings.summary: ensure_session does not wait for the transcript: warm_thread (first keystroke in the composer or a thread window) calls it while load_for_view's background read is still running, so the recap is built from an empty live.items. The message typed is queued until the history lands, but send_queued's ensure_session then returns early because commands already exist, so the agent answers with no conversation context.
findings.failure_scenario: A Claude Code thread that was rewound to a recap point (thread.reopen == Some(Reopen::Recap)) or that changed agent (native_id None) is opened after a relaunch. navigate -> load_for_view sets loading=true and reads rows in the background (a long thread takes a moment). The user starts typing at once: composer.rs 229 `ws.warm_up_in(&scope, cx)` -> warm_up -> warm_thread -> ensure_session: the guard at 3432 only checks commands/preparing/removing; `recap()` at 3442 reads `l.items` (empty) and is filtered to None; start_session runs with `resume: None, recap: None`. Return: send_as sees holds_messages (loading) and queues the text; the load callback calls send_queued -> send_to -> ensure_session, which returns at 3433 because `l.commands.is_some()`. The agent receives the message as the first turn of a brand-new session and knows nothing of the thread.
findings.evidence: workspace.rs 3430-3434: `fn ensure_session(...) { let Some(thread) = self.thread(id).cloned() else { return }; if self.live.get(id).is_some_and(|l| l.commands.is_some() || l.preparing || l.removing) { return; }` -- no `loading`/`!loaded` check. 3442: `let recap = || self.live.get(id).map(|l| trek_core::rewind::recap(&l.items)).filter(|r| !r.is_empty());` 3445: `Some(Reopen::Recap) => (None, None, false, recap()),` 3448: `None if thread.native_id.is_none() => (None, None, false, recap()),`. 3611-3616 warm_thread calls ensure_session for any non-Direct agent. 2526: `self.live.entry(id.to_string()).or_default().loading = true;` then the async read. 3406-3414 send_queued -> send_to -> send_as -> 3337 ensure_session (early return).
findings.suggested_fix: Have ensure_session (or warm_thread) return while `l.loading || !l.loaded`, and let the load callback warm the session once the history is in.

verdicts.reasoning: I traced the path in the working tree and found no guard. (1) load_for_view sets live.loading = true, then reads rows on a background task, so live.items stays empty until the callback runs. (2) The composer's Change handler calls warm_up_in once 2 or more characters are typed, not while editing, and not for a leading '/'. That goes to warm_thread. warm_thread only skips Direct agents and calls ensure_session. It never checks loaded or loading. (3) ensure_session returns early only on commands.is_some(), preparing or removing. It does not check loading. For Reopen::Recap, or for native_id == None, it builds the recap from live.items. That is empty, so recap() returns None and start_session gets resume None and recap None. attach() then sets commands. (4) send_as sees holds_messages (loading) and queues the text. The load callback sets loading = false and calls send_queued, which loops into send_to and send_as. send_as now calls ensure_session at ~3344, which returns because commands is Some. The prompt therefore goes to the already-running session that was started without a recap. I found no test that asserts this behaviour (the only warm_up test is agent_updates.rs, which is unrelated). The Reopen::Native case is not affected, because it resumes by session id. Only the Recap reopen and the native_id None cases are. These are narrower, but they are real, persisted states. The reopen column is stored, and a thread that changed agent has native_id None. The window is the duration of the background read, so it is mostly hit on long threads.

findings.title: Login PATH is read with `"$PATH"`, which fish expands space-joined, so fish users' agents get a PATH without /usr/bin and /bin
findings.summary: base_path() asks `$SHELL -ilc 'printf %s "$PATH"'`. In fish, PATH is a list and a list inside double quotes is joined with spaces, not colons, so the whole login PATH comes back as one space-separated string. compose_path then split_paths on ':' and keeps it as a single bogus entry; only extra_dirs (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, ...) are real. /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin and every folder fish added (nvm, volta, mise, pyenv shims...) are gone from login_path(), which is the PATH every agent and git call is spawned with.
findings.failure_scenario: SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/fish (a Homebrew fish user). Trek launches, base_path() returns "/opt/homebrew/bin /usr/local/bin /usr/bin /bin /usr/sbin /sbin". login_path() becomes that one entry plus the extras. detect::which("git") finds nothing unless Homebrew git is installed (git_binary() is Err → GitMissing toasts, worktree::git fails with 'couldn't run git' since it sets PATH=login_path()). Claude Code / Codex / ACP agents are spawned with PATH=login_path() (trek-agents/src/claude.rs:329, codex.rs:120, acp.rs:107), so their Bash tool can't find ls, cat, sed, python3 (/usr/bin, /bin missing), and any CLI installed via nvm/volta/mise is 'not installed' in Settings.
findings.evidence:
crates/trek-core/src/detect.rs:49-54:
    let shell = std::env::var("SHELL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/bin/zsh".into());
    shell_output(crate::procs::command(shell).args(["-ilc", "printf %s \"$PATH\""]), LOGIN_SHELL_TIMEOUT)
        .and_then(|o| String::from_utf8(o).ok())
        .map(|s| s.lines().last().unwrap_or_default().to_string())
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
crates/trek-core/src/detect.rs:175-177 (compose_path):
    let mut parts: Vec<PathBuf> = from.map(|p| std::env::split_paths(p).collect()).unwrap_or_default();
    parts.extend(extra_dirs(home));
extra_dirs (detect.rs:109-113) lists only ~/.local/bin, ~/.bun/bin, ~/.cargo/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin, ~/.opencode/bin, ~/.factory/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin: no /usr/bin or /bin.
Consumers: trek-agents/src/claude.rs:329 `.env("PATH", detect::login_path())`, trek-core/src/git.rs:90 `.env("PATH", crate::detect::login_path())`, trek-core/src/worktree.rs:49.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask for PATH in a shell-neutral way: run the login shell with `-ilc 'env'` (or `-ilc 'printf %s "$PATH"'` only for sh-family shells) and read the PATH= line, or exec `/usr/bin/env` from inside the login shell (`-ilc '/usr/bin/env'`) so the exported colon-joined value is what is read. Alternatively, when the returned string has no ':' but has spaces and SHELL ends in `fish`, split on whitespace. Also always append /usr/bin and /bin to extra_dirs as a safety net.

verdicts.reasoning: The code is quoted correctly. base_path() runs `$SHELL -ilc 'printf %s "$PATH"'`, and compose_path() splits the result on ':'. The claim fails on its factual premise about fish. Since fish 3.0 (2018), variables whose names end in PATH (PATH, CDPATH, MANPATH) are "path variables". Per the fish docs and changelog, I recall that these expand colon-joined when quoted ("$PATH"), and space-joined only when unquoted. So `printf %s "$PATH"` in current fish, including the Homebrew 3.x/4.x builds the scenario names, prints /opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:... and the split works. This is from memory, because fish isn't installed on this machine and I couldn't run it. Only fish older than 3.0 would space-join, and nobody installs that today. If the shell call fails, base_path() falls back to the process PATH, and the code has no test or intent that depends on fish. The reported scenario does not hold on current fish.
