findings.title: .tsx files are opened on the server with languageId "typescript"
findings.summary: spec() maps tsx, jsx and the *react ids onto the plain `typescript` and `javascript` language ids. Client::did_open sends that id as `languageId`. typescript-language-server derives the script kind from languageId (typescript is TS, typescriptreact is TSX), so a .tsx file is parsed as plain TypeScript.
findings.failure_scenario:
Open `App.tsx` containing `return
{x}
;` with typescript-language-server installed. The file is sent with languageId `typescript`, so JSX is parsed as TS type assertions. The gutter and Problems panel fill with bogus syntax errors on every React/TSX file, and hover and completion degrade.
findings.evidence: lsp_client.rs:25: `"ts" | "tsx" | "mts" | "cts" | "typescript" | "typescriptreact" => Some(("typescript-language-server", &["--stdio"], "typescript"))`; line 328: `"uri": uri, "languageId": self.lang`, where `lang` is that third tuple element (Client::start -> spawn(command, &root, language_id)). I could not inspect typescript-language-server's source locally, so the script-kind mapping is from memory.
findings.suggested_fix: Send the per-file language id (`typescriptreact` for tsx, `javascriptreact` for jsx) in did_open, while still sharing one server per root keyed on the server binary. For example pass the id into did_open instead of storing it on the Client.

findings.title: One malformed MCP server entry drops the whole `tools.mcp_servers` array, and the next add/save writes the file without the other servers
findings.summary: salvage() recurses only into tables; an array-of-tables value that fails to deserialize is dropped as a unit. For `[[tools.mcp_servers]]` that means one bad entry (a hand-edit, or a field a newer Trek wrote that this build can't read) empties the list in memory. to_toml() writes the raw array back only while the in-memory value still equals the default (empty); as soon as the user adds or edits any MCP server, the file is saved with just that server and every other previously configured server is gone for good (their Keychain tokens orphaned).
findings.failure_scenario: settings.toml has three [[tools.mcp_servers]] entries; the user hand-edits one to `enabled = "yes"` (or a newer Trek wrote a field with a type this version rejects, then the user downgrades). Launch: Settings::parse salvages, dropped = ["tools.mcp_servers"], the MCP list in Settings is empty and the toast names tools.mcp_servers. The user re-adds one server to get going → save() → to_toml(): value_at(tools.mcp_servers) != default (one entry vs none) → the raw array is not restored → the file now holds only the new server; the two good ones are lost.
findings.suggested_fix: In salvage(), when `v` is an Array whose elements are tables, probe each element on its own (path + index) and keep the ones that read, dropping only the bad elements; or at least record dropped array elements so to_toml can merge them back rather than replace the whole array.

findings.title: Manual pairing hint tells the user to type 8 fingerprint characters when 16 are required
findings.summary: When the typed fingerprint doesn't validate, the hint says "8 characters, 0–9 and A–F", but `Fingerprint.typedPrefix` only accepts exactly `typedLength = 16` hex characters (the placeholder shows the 16-character `ABCD-1234-EF56-7890` form). A user who follows the hint can never pair over TLS by hand.
findings.failure_scenario: User types the first 8 hex characters of the fingerprint shown on the Mac (as the hint instructs). `fingerprintInvalid` stays true, the Pair button stays disabled, and the hint keeps saying 8 characters; the only way forward is to clear the field and pair unencrypted or guess that 16 are needed.
findings.evidence: ios/Trek/Views/PairingView.swift:180-183 `private var fingerprintHint: String { fingerprintInvalid ? "8 characters, 0–9 and A–F, as your Mac shows it." : … }`; :176-178 `fingerprintInvalid … Fingerprint.typedPrefix(fingerprint) == nil`; :165 `.disabled(… || fingerprintInvalid)`. ios/Trek/Net/TrekClient.swift:46 `static let typedLength = 16`; :62-65 `typedPrefix … hex.count == typedLength && hex.allSatisfy(\.isHexDigit) ? hex : nil`.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the hint to "16 characters, 0–9 and A–F (four groups of four), as your Mac shows it." or derive the count from `Fingerprint.typedLength`.

findings.title: Source Control drops the next changed file after a rename whose old path is 3 characters or fewer
findings.summary: The `status --porcelain=v1 -z` parser filters entries with `.filter(|e| e.len() > 3)` and, on `R`/`C`, calls `entries.next()` to skip the old-path entry. That entry has no `XY ` prefix. When the old path is 3 bytes or fewer (e.g. `a.c`) it is already filtered out, so `entries.next()` swallows the following real status entry instead.
findings.failure_scenario: In a repo, `git mv a.c b.c` and also modify `zzzz.txt`. Raw output (confirmed with git): `R  b.c|a.c| M zzzz.txt|`. The filter removes `a.c`, `R` consumes ` M zzzz.txt`, and zzzz.txt never appears in Changes. Select-all Stage/Commit-all state and the activity badge count are then wrong.
findings.evidence: scm.rs:78-84: `let mut entries = out.split(|b| *b == 0).filter(|e| e.len() > 3); while let Some(e) = entries.next() { ... if x == 'R' || x == 'C' { entries.next(); }`
findings.suggested_fix: Split without the length filter (skip only empty entries) so the old-path entry is always consumed, or consume the old path from an unfiltered iterator before applying the length filter.

findings.title: A folded/literal YAML description (`description: >-` or `|`) is read as the literal text '>-', so the Skills page shows '>-' instead of the description
findings.summary: read_front_matter takes the text after `description:` on the same line as the value. For the YAML block-scalar forms the same line holds only the indicator (`>-`, `>`, `|`), so desc becomes Some(">-") and the real text on the following indented lines is ignored. Three of the user's own skills on this machine use this form.
findings.failure_scenario:
~/.agents/skills/orchestration/SKILL.md begins:
---
name: orchestration
description: >-
  Coordinate supervised Orca workers: threaded messages, ...
---
Settings > Skills lists 'orchestration' with the description '>-' (settings_view/pages.rs:1218 renders skill.description), and searching the skills list for 'Orca' (pages.rs:1150 matches on description) does not find it. Same for ~/.agents/skills/computer-use and orca-cli.
findings.suggested_fix: When the value is one of `>`, `>-`, `|`, `|-`, `|+`, `>+`, collect the following lines while they are indented, strip the indentation, and join them with a space (for `>`) or newline (for `|`).

findings.title: `program()` mis-parses `timeout` options that take a value, so `timeout -s KILL 60 ./scripts/app check` is not counted as a verification run
findings.summary: The `timeout` prefix handling skips every leading `-flag` word and then at most one duration-looking word, but `-s SIG` and `-k DUR` take a value; the value is left as the first word, so the real program is never reached and `invocations()` finds nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent runs `timeout -s KILL 60 ./scripts/app check` (or `timeout -k 5 60 ./scripts/app check`) in a Bash tool call; `program()` returns ["KILL", "60", "./scripts/app", "check"], `invocations()` tests `is("KILL", needle)` (false) and breaks because "KILL" is not in RUNNERS, so `verdict()` returns None for the turn: thread_view.rs:1414 shows the turn as unverified and workspace/verification.rs:218 does not count the CLI as having been run, even though it ran and passed. The plain `timeout 60 sh scripts/app check` form is tested and works, which shows the intent is to see through `timeout`.
findings.suggested_fix: When skipping `timeout`'s options, consume the value of `-s`/`--signal` and `-k`/`--kill-after` (and `--signal=`/`--kill-after=` forms need no extra skip), e.g. `if matches!(w, "-s" | "-k" | "--signal" | "--kill-after") { i += 1 }` inside the flag loop, then skip the duration as now.

findings.title: "Ask Trek about selection" reports the cursor line as the selection's start, so a downward selection is labelled with only its last line
findings.summary: For the `ask` command the extension sends `line = sel.active.line + 1` and `end = sel.end.line + 1`. `active` is the cursor end of the selection; when a selection is made top-to-bottom (the usual drag or shift+down), active == end, so Trek receives line == end and its `(Some(l), Some(e)) if e > l` check falls through to a single-line label.
findings.failure_scenario: Select lines 5–12 of main.rs by dragging downward and run "Ask Trek about selection". The link carries `line=12&end=12`. deep_link::follow builds `where_` as `L12` instead of `L5-L12`, so the composer header reads `main.rs L12` above an 8-line snippet, and an agent told to look at line 12 is pointed at the end of the selection. Selecting the same lines upward (anchor at 12, cursor at 5) gives `L5-L12`, so the label depends on the drag direction.
findings.suggested_fix: For `ask`, send `line = sel.start.line + 1` (keep `sel.active` for `edit`, where the caret is what matters).

findings.title: Sidebar dates older than a week are formatted in UTC, not the user's local time
findings.summary: `relative` formats the 'Sep 12' fallback straight from the UTC `DateTime`. Every other function in the file (`until`, `clock`, `reset_clock`) converts to `Local` first.
findings.failure_scenario: A user in UTC-8 touches a thread or note at 17:00 local on Sep 11. That is 01:00 UTC on Sep 12, so after a week the sidebar and notes list show 'Sep 12', one day later than the user's own date. East of UTC the date is one day early for late-night activity.
findings.evidence: time.rs:13: `_ => chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(ms).map(|d| d.format("%b %-d").to_string()).unwrap_or_default()` versus time.rs:41 `d.with_timezone(&chrono::Local).format(...)`.
findings.suggested_fix: `.map(|d| d.with_timezone(&chrono::Local).format("%b %-d").to_string())`.

findings.title: Explorer rename refuses a case-only rename on macOS: 'already exists'
findings.summary: commit_edit only short-circuits when the new name equals the old name byte-for-byte; otherwise name_problem() checks `dir.join(name).symlink_metadata().is_ok()`, which on the default case-insensitive APFS succeeds for the file being renamed itself when only the case differs, so the rename is rejected with a toast and the edit stays open.
findings.failure_scenario: In the editor's Explorer right-click `readme.md` -> Rename…, type `README.md`, press Enter. name_problem sees `dir/README.md` exists (it is the same file; verified `touch Foo; stat foo` succeeds on APFS) and shows 'A file or folder “README.md” already exists here. Choose another name.' The user cannot change a file's case from Trek even though `std::fs::rename` would do it.
findings.suggested_fix: For EditKind::Rename, skip the exists check when the target resolves to the source (same `from.canonicalize()` or `fs::metadata` dev/ino, or when `from.file_name()` equals the new name case-insensitively on a case-insensitive volume), and let fs::rename run.

findings.title: IDE terminal list labels every shell "zsh N" whatever shell is configured
findings.summary: When more than one terminal is open, the panel's list names them with a hard-coded `zsh`. The chat terminal dock correctly uses shell_name(settings.terminal.shell).
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows (PowerShell/cmd) or macOS with bash/fish, or with `settings.terminal.shell` set, open two terminals in the IDE panel. The right-hand list shows `zsh 1`, `zsh 2`, which misnames the shells.
findings.evidence: panel.rs:253 `.child(format!("zsh {}", ix + 1))`; contrast terminal_dock.rs `let shell = crate::panels::terminal::shell_name(&self.workspace.read(cx).settings.terminal.shell);` and `format!("{shell} {}", ix + 1)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use crate::panels::terminal::shell_name(&settings.terminal.shell) as the dock does.

findings.title: `trek-dev.ps1 check` always reports `screenshots: null` because $shots is set in a child scope
findings.summary: Invoke-Check assigns `$shots` inside the scriptblock passed to With-Lock, which runs it with `& $Body` in a new child scope. `Out-Result` after With-Lock reads the function-scope `$shots`, which was never assigned.
findings.failure_scenario: After a successful `trek-dev.ps1 check`, the JSON has `"screenshots": null` even though two PNGs were captured. The Python driver returns the list, so any caller that reads the top-level `screenshots` field on Windows gets nothing. The paths are only in the steps array.
findings.evidence: line 300 `With-Lock {`; line 325 `$shots = @()`; line 335 `$shots += (Join-Path $art "$name.png")`; line 340 `Out-Result @{ passed = $true; quick = $Quick; steps = $steps; screenshots = $shots }`; line 107 `try { & $Body } finally { $stream.Dispose() }`
findings.suggested_fix: Initialise `$shots` before `With-Lock` and assign it with `$script:shots`, or return the value from the scriptblock.

findings.title: `script/capture.sh <suite>` (bare name) exits 1 after a successful mac run
findings.summary: The default case arm is `[[ -f media/mac/$1.cmds ]] && run_mac "$1"; [[ -f media/ios/$1.list ]] && run_ios "$1"`. When only the mac manifest exists, the second test is false, so the arm's status, and the script's, is 1. A name that matches nothing exits 1 silently.
findings.failure_scenario: `script/capture.sh smoke` captures everything and prints "published", then exits 1, so a CI step or `&&` chain treats it as failed. A typo such as `script/capture.sh smok` prints nothing at all. I reproduced the exit status with an equivalent zsh snippet under `set -euo pipefail` (rc=1).
findings.evidence: capture.sh:155 `*) [[ -f media/mac/$1.cmds ]] && run_mac "$1"; [[ -f media/ios/$1.list ]] && run_ios "$1";;`
findings.suggested_fix: Use if/elif with an explicit `die "no suite named $1"` fallback so the success path ends in status 0.

findings.title: The settings scroll container has no test id, so `trek-dev control scroll settings-content` always fails
findings.summary: The scroll container is `div().id("settings-content")...overflow_y_scroll()` without `.test_support()`, so the shots driver cannot find it. Nothing below the first screen of a long settings page (for example Computer use > Work in the background > Show what they're doing on Tools & MCP) can be reached by the documented CLI path.
findings.failure_scenario: `trek-dev open settings:tools-&-mcp; trek-dev control scroll settings-content 700` fails with 'hover: nothing on screen is settings-content', and `control click background-pip` fails with 'hidden or scrolled away'. It only works by scrolling over some other visible id (`control scroll computer-use 600`).
findings.evidence: The log shows `shot command failed: scroll settings-content 700: hover: nothing on screen is settings-content`. The line at settings_view.rs:1655 has no `.test_support()`, unlike the ids at lines 186, 581 and 1124.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `.test_support()` to the `settings-content` div, and note in skills-mcp-and-computer-use.md how to reach the Computer use rows.

findings.title: toggle_block on an empty line does nothing: a list/heading/quote can't be started on a blank line
findings.summary: `all` is computed over the non-blank lines only; when the cursor's line is blank there are none, so `all()` is vacuously true and the code takes the 'already a block, strip the marker' branch, which strips nothing. Turning a blank line (a new note, the line after a paragraph) into a bullet, checklist, numbered item, heading or quote leaves it unchanged; the user has to type a character first.
findings.failure_scenario: New empty note (body ""), user presses the bullet-list shortcut/toolbar button: toggle_block("", 0..0, Block::Bullets). lines = [""]; `all` = iter().filter(non-blank).all(..) == true; map: `l.trim().is_empty() && lines.len() > 1` is false, so the `if all` branch runs with cut = marker_len("", Bullets).unwrap_or(0) = 0 and returns "" unchanged. Same for a blank line between two paragraphs (sel on it) and for Heading(n)/Checklist/Quote. Nothing happens on screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a selection whose lines are all blank as 'not a block': e.g. `let all = lines.iter().any(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()) && lines.iter().filter(..).all(..)`, so a blank line gets the marker ("- ", "# ", "- [ ] ", "> "). Add a test: toggle_block("", 0..0, Block::Bullets).text == "- " with selection 2..2.

findings.title: Changelog cache is not keyed by feed, so a feed switch or non-GitHub feed shows another feed's release notes
findings.summary: `fetch` falls back to the single on-disk `changelog.json` whenever `fetch_live` errors, including the deliberate `bail!("this update feed has no release list")` for non-GitHub feeds and a fetch of a different GitHub repo; the cache records nothing about which feed produced it, so the Updates page shows release notes from whatever feed was fetched last.
findings.failure_scenario: User runs Trek with the default feed once (cache filled with dokyit/Trek releases), then sets Settings > Updates > feed_url to a private manifest such as `https://example.com/trek.json` or a fork's `https://github.com/someone/fork/releases`. The next `changelog::fetch` bails (no release list) or fails (fork offline/404), `cached()` returns the official list, and `updater::pending_changes` (updater.rs:297) runs `changelog::between(&self.changelog, …, &offer.version)` over it: an update to 0.5.0 from the private feed shows dokyit/Trek's 0.5.0 notes as "what's new", and `installed_release` shows the official notes for the running fork build. The module's stated intent is only to reuse "the copy saved by the last fetch when GitHub can't be reached" for the same feed.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the repo (or full feed URL) alongside the cached list (e.g. a `{repo, releases}` wrapper, or name the file after the repo) and only return the cache when it matches `github_repo(updates)`; when `github_repo` is None, return Err without consulting the cache.

findings.title: Attaching non-image files via the + menu moves the caret to the start of the message
findings.summary: Composer::attach appends `@path` references by rebuilding the whole value with TextareaState::set_value, which for a multi-line input resets the selection to 0..0. The next keystrokes land at the beginning of the message rather than after the appended references.
findings.failure_scenario: Type "please review ", open + -> "Add photos & files", pick notes.md. The text becomes "please review @/Users/me/notes.md " but the caret is at offset 0; typing "thanks" yields "thanksplease review @/Users/me/notes.md ". (add_paths for drag-and-drop and attachments::paste use insert() and keep the caret, so only this path misbehaves.)
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the references at the caret with `s.insert(...)` as add_paths does, or call `s.set_selected_range(len..len, cx)` after set_value.

findings.title: Any web page can spoof the Browser tool's address bar via the `url` IPC message
findings.summary: handle_ipc accepts `{t:'url', url:...}` from any non-internal origin and writes it straight into `tab.page.url` without checking it against the view's real URL. The IPC channel (`window.ipc.postMessage`) is available to every page, so a page can display an arbitrary address in the URL pill, the tab label/host, 'Copy URL' and 'Open in default browser'.
findings.failure_scenario: Navigate to a page containing `window.ipc.postMessage(JSON.stringify({t:'url', url:'https://github.com/login'}))`. The URL pill shows github.com/login with the lock icon while the view still shows the attacker's page; 'Copy URL' copies the fake address; 'Open in default browser' opens the fake one. Trek's own INIT_JS only sends the real location, but nothing enforces that.
findings.suggested_fix: Ignore the message body's url and read the real one: `tab.view.read(cx).raw().url()` (wry exposes it; sync_theme/scan_servers already use it), or at least require `host_of(url) == host_of(origin)` before accepting it.

findings.title: ⌘P then ⌘K (or the reverse) overwrites `restore` with the palette's own input, so Esc leaves nothing focused
findings.summary: show() unconditionally records `window.focused()` as the focus to restore. toggle()/toggle_files() call show() again when the palette is already open in the other mode, at which point the focused handle is the palette's input. dismiss() then 'restores' focus to the input and immediately blurs it, so the editor/composer that had focus before the palette opened never gets it back.
findings.failure_scenario: In the editor with the cursor in a file press ⌘P (Quick Open opens, restore = editor), then ⌘K (toggle: open && files_only, so else-branch -> show(): restore = palette input), then Esc. dismiss() focuses the palette input, sees it contains focus and calls window.blur(). Keyboard focus is now nowhere; typing does nothing until the user clicks the editor again.
findings.suggested_fix: In show(), only capture `restore` when `!self.open` (or when the currently focused handle isn't the palette's input).

findings.title: app_pid parses an lsappinfo output format that macOS 27 does not produce, so windowless apps never get a pid
findings.summary: `app_pid` assumes `lsappinfo info -only pid <name>` prints `"pid"=1234` and parses the text after the last `=`. On this machine (Darwin 27.2) the output is a multi-line dump ending in `Arch=!!none`, with the pid shown as `pid = 698 ...`. The parse always fails and returns None.
findings.failure_scenario: In background mode the agent calls open_app on an app that has no window yet, such as a menu-bar app or an app that opens windowless. `bg_open_app` times out its window wait and calls `app_pid(name)`. That returns None, so the agent gets the error 'Opened X, but no window of it has appeared yet.' and the windowless-target path (keys reach the app, cmd+n) is never reached. The old target also stays set, so later clicks go to the previous window.
findings.evidence: macos.rs:241-243: `run_ok("/usr/bin/lsappinfo", &["info","-only","pid",name] ...)` then `// "pid"=1234` and `out.rsplit('=').next()?.trim().parse().ok()`. Running `lsappinfo info -only pid Ollama` here prints `pid = 1348 !cgsConnection !signalled type=[ NULL ]  flavor=[ NULL ]  Version=[ NULL ]  Arch=!!none`. The text after the last '=' is '!!none', which does not parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Find the pid another way: `lsappinfo find name=<app>` and then a keyed query, or a regex for `pid\s*=\s*(\d+)`, or NSWorkspace/`pgrep -x`. Also clear `self.target` when the open fails.

findings.title: Anthropic direct sessions are told they have tools but the request sends none
findings.summary: system_prompt tells every direct session it has bash/read_file/write_file/edit_file, but anthropic_body never includes a `tools` array and anthropic_turn always returns `tool_calls: vec![]`. A session on the "Anthropic API" provider therefore cannot inspect or change the project, while its instructions claim it can.
findings.failure_scenario: User adds an Anthropic API key, picks a Claude model as a direct provider and asks "fix the failing test in src/parser.rs". The request carries the system prompt listing four tools and no `tools` field; the model either says it cannot access files or writes pseudo tool-call text in its answer. Nothing is read or edited; the OpenAI-wire providers in the same adapter do run tools.
findings.evidence: direct.rs:25-33 system_prompt: `You have access to tools to inspect files, make code edits, and execute terminal commands.\n - bash: ... - read_file: ... - write_file: ... - edit_file: ...`. direct.rs:917-923 anthropic_body: `json!({ "model": model, "max_tokens": 64000, "stream": true, "system": system, "messages": history })` with no `tools`. direct.rs:1035-1039 anthropic_turn returns `TurnResponse { text, content: Some(...), tool_calls: vec![] }`. openai_turn by contrast sends `"tools": direct_tools()` (direct.rs:1070-1075). catalog.rs:120 lists `anthropic` with `wire: Wire::Anthropic`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either pass direct_tools() in Anthropic's tool schema and parse tool_use blocks, or drop the tool paragraph from the system prompt for Wire::Anthropic.

findings.title: load_for_view recreates a LiveThread for a thread deleted while its history was being read
findings.summary: The load callback writes the spend into `self.live.entry(id).or_default()` before checking whether the thread still exists. delete_thread removed the live entry (with its gone-flagged git guard), so a fresh default LiveThread under the dead id is created and kept for the rest of the run.
findings.failure_scenario: Open a long thread (load_for_view starts its background read), delete it from the sidebar before the read lands (delete_thread 5202 `self.live.remove(&t.id)`). The callback runs: 2546-2556 `this.live.entry(id.clone()).or_default().spend = Some(spend)` recreates the entry; 2557-2561 then finds it and returns at `if this.thread(&id).is_none() { return; }`, leaving an orphan LiveThread with a new, non-gone GitGuard in `live` (counted by reap_idle_sessions/work_in_flight loops, never cleaned).
findings.evidence: workspace.rs 2546-2561: `if let Some((own, subs, theirs)) = spend_data { ... this.live.entry(id.clone()).or_default().spend = Some(spend); } let Some(live) = this.live.get_mut(&id) else { return }; live.loading = false; // Deleted while it was read: nothing is left to show it in. if this.thread(&id).is_none() { return; }`. 5202-5205 in delete_thread: `if let Some(live) = self.live.remove(&t.id) { live.git_guard.gone.store(true, ...); guards.push(live.git_guard.clone()); }`.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `this.thread(&id).is_none()` (and that the live entry still exists) before touching `self.live.entry(...)` in the callback.

findings.title: Tray menu's "Background Use" item starts greyed out when the tray is (re)created during an active background session
findings.summary: `Tray::new` syncs the glyph and status line initially but never calls `sync_behind`. The new item is created disabled with the "Show" label and is only updated when `BackgroundUse` next notifies.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent is using the computer in the background (sessions non-empty, PiP showing). The user toggles Settings > Notifications > Menu bar icon off and then on. The new tray menu shows a disabled "Show Background Use" while the picture is on screen. It stays wrong until the next step or sweep notifies `BackgroundUse`, and the user cannot use the menu to hide the PiP. The same applies to the Windows tray.
findings.evidence: tray.rs:176 `let behind = MenuItem::new(SHOW_BEHIND, false, None);`; :262-264 `let mut this = Self {...}; let state = Self::read_state(workspace.read(cx), cx); this.sync(state, cx); this` with no `this.sync_behind(background_use.read(cx))`; `sync_behind` (:282) is called only from `cx.observe(&background_use, ...)`.
findings.suggested_fix: After constructing `this`, call `this.sync_behind(workspace.read(cx).background_use.read(cx))`.

findings.title: File icon and chip colour lookups split paths only on '/', so Windows paths pick the wrong icon
findings.summary: icon_name, folder_icon_name and type_colour take the file name with `rsplit('/')`. A backslash path is treated as one long name. Whole-name entries (Cargo.toml, README.md, Dockerfile, LICENSE, package-lock.json, Makefile) then never match, and the suffix scan starts at the first '.' anywhere in the path.
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows the composer's context chip calls `file_icon::badge(&path.to_string_lossy(), ...)` (ide/ai/input.rs, ContextChip::File). For `C:\proj\Cargo.toml` the name lookup misses, so the generic toml icon shows instead of the cargo icon. `C:\proj\README.md` shows the markdown icon instead of readme. `C:\proj\Dockerfile` has no '.', so it shows `_file` instead of docker. type_colour does the same: `web\package-lock.json` is coloured as JSON instead of staying neutral, and `build\Makefile` loses its colour. Unix paths are unaffected.
findings.evidence: file_icon.rs:130-134: `let name = path.trim_end_matches('/').rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(path); if let Some(icon) = find(&icons.names, name)...`. The same pattern is in type_colour (line 13) and folder_icon_name. The caller is ide/ai/input.rs:647: `ContextChip::File { path } => crate::file_icon::badge(&path.to_string_lossy(), px(11.), cx)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Split on both separators: `path.trim_end_matches(['/', '\\']).rsplit(['/', '\\']).next()` in icon_name, folder_icon_name and type_colour. Alternatively pass file_name() at the call site.

findings.title: update-e2e.sh runs `rm -rf` on $TREK_E2E_DIR with no check that it is a scratch folder
findings.summary: The script deletes $WORK at the start and again in cleanup, and WORK comes straight from TREK_E2E_DIR. The PowerShell twin refuses a non-empty folder that lacks a `.trek-update-e2e` marker; the shell version has no such guard.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone sets `TREK_E2E_DIR=~/Documents/e2e` (an existing folder with their files) or points it at a shared directory. `rm -rf "$WORK"; mkdir -p ...` wipes it on startup, and cleanup wipes it again after the run.
findings.evidence: update-e2e.sh:26 `WORK=${TREK_E2E_DIR:-/tmp/trek-update-e2e}`, :46 `rm -rf "$WORK"; mkdir -p "$WORK/app" "$WORK/serve" "$WORK/data"`, :41 `rm -rf "$WORK"` in cleanup; compare update-e2e.ps1:112-115 which throws unless the folder is empty or has the marker
findings.suggested_fix: Port the marker-file guard: refuse a non-empty $WORK that has no `.trek-update-e2e`, and touch the marker after creating it.

findings.title: Basecamp Projects table hides the project name when the right panel is open
findings.summary: With the right panel open the Basecamp column is narrow. The Project column is squeezed to a few pixels while the numeric columns keep their full width, so the project name shows as '...'.
findings.failure_scenario: Run `trek-dev open tool:git; trek-dev open basecamp; trek-dev screenshot bc`. The Projects rows read 'No p...', 'TR ...' and '21 ...': the 'Trek' project cannot be told from the others, while the Threads/Turns/Tokens/Cost/Failures columns have plenty of unused space.
findings.evidence: Screenshot /tmp/sim-later.png (Basecamp with the Simulator tab open): Projects rows 'No p... 16 18 211K', 'TR ... 8 10 117K', '21 ... 0 1 12K'. The same table at full width (/tmp/r-basecamp.png) shows 'Trek' and 'No project' in full.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the name column flex-grow with a minimum width and let the numeric columns shrink or hide (Cost) at narrow widths.

findings.title: Windows tray menu gets a permanently disabled 'Show Background Use' item
findings.summary: `build()` adds the 'Show Background Use' MenuItem unconditionally. Background use never runs on Windows: `trek_mcp_env` returns no env there, and `Computer` falls back to Front mode. The item stays disabled forever on the Windows tray menu.
findings.failure_scenario: A Windows user opens the tray icon menu and sees a greyed-out 'Show Background Use' entry under 'No agents running'. It can never be enabled, because `sync_behind` enables it only when `sessions` is non-empty and sessions are only reported by background-mode `trek-mcp computer`.
findings.evidence: tray.rs:168 `let behind = MenuItem::new(SHOW_BEHIND, false, None);` and the `menu.append_items(&[&status, &behind, ...` change, with no `cfg`/`is_windows()` guard. workspace.rs `trek_mcp_env`: `if family == "computer" && background && !windows`. settings_view.rs hides the setting on Windows ('Windows' work in front').
findings.suggested_fix: Only append the `behind` item when `!crate::words::is_windows()`, or on `cfg(target_os = "macos")`.

findings.title: A port or reach changed while the phone server is starting is silently ignored until the next settings save
findings.summary: start_remote captures port and reach when it is spawned and records them as started_with when it finishes; sync_remote ignores calls while remote_starting is true and nothing re-runs sync_remote after the start completes, so a port/reach changed during the (up to several seconds) startup leaves the server on the old address until some unrelated settings change triggers save_settings.
findings.failure_scenario: Trek launches with the phone server on; start_remote runs host_info() (scutil), Addresses::find() (up to two 2 s tailscale CLI calls) and the bind loop. During that window the user opens Settings > Phone and changes the port 7420 -> 7430 (each edit calls save_settings -> sync_remote, which hits the `_ => {}` arm because remote is None and remote_starting is true). The start finishes and stores started_with = (7420, reach). The server listens and advertises on 7420; Settings shows the pairing code with the old port, and the phone paired to 7430 can't connect, until any other setting is saved.
findings.suggested_fix: At the end of the `this.update` closure in start_remote (after ws.remote is set and remote_starting cleared), call ws.sync_remote(cx) so a changed (port, reach) restarts it immediately.

findings.title: The composer clears the typed message and photos before the Mac acknowledges the send; any send error loses them
findings.summary: `ComposerArea.send()` only guards on `model.connection == .connected`, then calls `model.send` and immediately empties `composer.draft` and `composer.photos`. `AppModel.send` uses `act`, whose only error handling is a toast. A connection drop between the check and delivery, an oversized frame, or any error reply from the Mac (bad_request, host_error, not_found for a thread deleted on the Mac) therefore discards what the user typed, contradicting the comment that what's typed stays in the composer when it can't go.
findings.failure_scenario: User types a long message in a thread; the Mac deletes/archives that thread (or Wi-Fi drops) a moment before they tap send. `connection` is still `.connected`, so the guard passes, the frame goes out (or is queued on a dying socket), and `composer.draft = ""` runs. The Mac answers with an error (or failPending fires on the drop) → `show(text, error: true)` toast for 3 seconds. The message text is irrecoverable.
findings.evidence: ios/Trek/Views/ThreadView.swift:640-644 `// Nothing can go while the Mac is out of reach: what's typed stays in the composer. guard model.connection == .connected else { … return }`; :651-654 `model.send(…); composer.draft = ""; composer.photos = []`. ios/Trek/Model/AppModel.swift:531-536 `func send … act(.send(…)) { … }`; :407-411 `func act … if case .error(_, _, let text) = reply { self?.show(text, error: true) }`; :400-403 `failPending` turns a dropped connection into the same error reply.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear the draft only in the ack path of `act`/`send` (restore it on error), or keep the text in a pending-send slot until the Mac acknowledges.
findings.reason: clearing the composer on send is optimistic by design; restoring after a drop could duplicate a delivered message; the oversized-frame cause is fixed by ios-01

findings.title: Removing an added agent while its update installs re-adds it when the install finishes
findings.summary: The settings row's ellipsis menu offers "Remove…" at all times, including while `installs` holds `Install::Running` for an update of that agent. `remove_added_agent` drops it from settings, clears `installs`, and spawns `registry::remove` (rm -rf of the agent's folder) while `registry::install` is still unpacking into that same folder on the runtime. When the install task then sends `Step::Done(Ok(added))`, the handler unconditionally calls `put_added`, which pushes the agent back into `settings.added_agents`, saves settings and toasts "X is up to date", undoing the removal; its on-disk files may have been deleted under it.
findings.failure_scenario: Settings › Agents: a registry agent shows "Update to 1.2"; user clicks it (row shows "Downloading 40%"), then opens the row menu → Remove… → Remove. Toast "Removed X", the row disappears, `remove_dir_all(agents_dir/X)` runs concurrently with `download_and_unpack` into `agents_dir/X/1.2`. Seconds later the install completes: `put_added` re-inserts X into settings with `command` pointing at a binary that `registry::remove` may have deleted, toast "X is ready in Trek", and the agent is back in the list, possibly broken (binary missing) until re-installed.
findings.evidence: added_agents.rs:170-189: `while let Ok(step) = rx.recv().await { … Step::Done(Ok(added)) => { this.added_agents.installs.remove(&id); … let updated = this.settings.added_agents.iter().any(|a| a.id == added.id); this.put_added(added, cx); cx.emit(WorkspaceEvent::Toast { message: if updated { … } else { format!("{name} is ready in Trek") } … }` — no check that the agent is still wanted. added_agents.rs:222-234 `remove_added_agent`: `self.settings.added_agents.remove(at); … self.added_agents.installs.remove(id); … trek_core::runtime().spawn_blocking(move || registry::remove(&agent));`. registry.rs:536-539 `remove` → `std::fs::remove_dir_all(agents_dir().join(&agent.id))`; registry.rs:671-691 `install` writes into `agents_dir().join(&agent.id)` / `home.join(&agent.version)`. settings_view.rs:930 `menu.item(PopupMenuItem::new("Remove…").on_click(… confirm_remove …))` with no `installs` gate.
findings.suggested_fix: In the `Step::Done(Ok(added))` arm, only call `put_added` if the install is still expected (e.g. `this.added_agents.installs.get(&id)` is still `Install::Running` for this install, or the agent is still in `settings.added_agents` for an update); otherwise call `registry::remove(&added)` on the runtime and drop it. Also hide or disable Remove… in the row menu while `installs[id]` is `Running`.

findings.title: Attached pictures and files are inserted into whichever note is open when the copy finishes
findings.summary: `add_images` copies the files on a background task, then in the completion calls `this.apply(notes::insert_lines(&text, sel, ...))` on the editor's current text. It never checks that the note that was open when the attach started is still the current one.
findings.failure_scenario: The user drops a multi-GB video, or a HEIC that needs conversion, into note A. While it copies they click note B. When the copy finishes, the `[video](attachments/…)` link is written into B at B's cursor and B is saved. A gets nothing, and B is modified without the user asking.
findings.evidence: notes.rs:446-461: the `update_in` closure does `let (text, sel) = Self::read(&this.editor, cx); this.apply(notes::insert_lines(&text, sel, &lines.join("\n")), window, cx);` with no comparison against the note id captured before the spawn.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture `self.current.clone()` before spawning. In the completion, only insert if it still matches. Otherwise append the links to that note's body on disk, or toast that the attachment was kept but not linked.
findings.reason: add_images documents inserting into the note open when the copy finishes; design edge case

findings.title: Pairing QR/code stays on screen after it expires, still labelled "works once, for about 1 min"
findings.summary: The page clamps the remaining time with `.max(0) + 1` and never checks expiry. `remote.offer` is cleared only on a successful pairing or Cancel, so an expired offer stays displayed as valid.
findings.failure_scenario: The user opens "Show pairing code" and leaves it for longer than the TTL. The QR and code remain, captioned "Address … · works once, for about 1 min". Scanning or typing it on the phone fails because the server's pairing code has expired. Nothing tells the user to press New code.
findings.evidence: mobile.rs:218 `let left = ((offer.expires_at - trek_core::store::now_ms()) / 60_000).max(0) + 1;` and the caption `works once, for about {left} min`; remote.rs clears `remote.offer = None` only at :561 (cancel) and :1511 (`ServerNotice::Paired`), and `expires_at` is set only in trek-remote/src/server.rs:234.
findings.suggested_fix: When `offer.expires_at <= now`, show "Expired" with a New code button, or clear `remote.offer` on a timer.

findings.title: Thread writes are stale-copy overwrites, so a concurrent import's changes are silently reverted
findings.summary: Store::update_thread and the app's save_thread write a whole Thread row built from a copy read earlier; nothing holds the connection lock between read and write. The launch-time import runs on the background executor and commits retitles and archives (upsert_imported, hide_missing) in its own transactions, so a main-thread save of a copy loaded before those commits writes the old title, imported_title, archived_at and import_hidden back.
findings.failure_scenario: At launch workspace.rs:1331 starts import_threads, which runs trek_core::import::import_all on the background executor for several seconds on a large Claude/Codex history. hide_missing (store.rs:1078-1104) archives an imported thread T whose session file was deleted, setting archived_at and import_hidden='deleted', and upsert_one retitles another thread U. The sidebar still shows the launch-time list, so the user clicks T; workspace.rs:1732 calls mutate_thread, which runs save_thread(t) (workspace.rs:1829) with the launch-time copy of T: archived_at=NULL, import_hidden=NULL, old title. The upsert at store.rs:748 overwrites every column, so T reappears unarchived with no record that its session is gone, and U's new title/imported_title are lost; the import summary reports 'gone: 1' and 'retitled: 1' that are no longer true. Imports only run at launch or on request, so the wrong state persists until the next one.
findings.evidence: store.rs:828-833: `pub fn update_thread(&self, id: &str, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Thread)) -> Result<Option<Thread>> { let Some(mut t) = self.thread(id)? else { return Ok(None) }; f(&mut t); self.save_thread(&t)?; Ok(Some(t)) }` (thread() and save_thread() each take and release the lock separately). store.rs:741-748: `fn save_thread_in(...)` builds `INSERT INTO threads (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET {c} = excluded.{c}` for every column. store.rs:1095-1101: hide_missing does `UPDATE threads SET archived_at = ?2, import_hidden = ?3 WHERE id = ?1` inside its own transaction. workspace.rs:6093: `cx.background_executor().spawn(async move { trek_core::import::import_all(&store, &settings) })`; workspace.rs:1823-1831: mutate_thread mutates the in-memory copy and calls `self.store.save_thread(t)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Make update_thread read-modify-write inside one transaction on the held connection (lock once, SELECT, apply f, UPDATE, commit), and have the app route field changes through it rather than saving whole in-memory copies; or re-read the row in save_thread and only write the columns the caller changed.
findings.reason: import_threads calls reload() when the import finishes; the stale-copy window needs the user to act on that thread during the launch-time import, and a store-level change cannot close it because the app saves whole in-memory copies

findings.title: A phone's changes that arrive while the note is dirty are never loaded afterwards
findings.summary: The workspace observer stores the new `notes_epoch` into `self.epoch` first, then calls `reload`, which returns immediately when `dirty`. Once the 400 ms save flushes, nothing re-triggers a reload, because the epoch already matches. The in-memory list stays stale for every other note until the phone changes something again.
findings.failure_scenario: The Mac user is typing in note A (dirty) when the phone creates note C and edits note B. `reload` is skipped and the epoch is consumed. After the save, C is missing from the list and B shows its old body. If the user opens B and types, the Mac saves B's stale text plus the edit over the phone's change.
findings.evidence: notes.rs:211-215: `if epoch != this.epoch { this.epoch = epoch; this.reload(window, cx); }` and notes.rs:271: `fn reload(...) { if self.dirty { return; } ...`. `flush` (notes.rs:368) never reloads.
findings.suggested_fix: Only record the epoch after a reload really happens, or remember a pending reload and run it at the end of `flush`.

findings.title: Inno installer defaults to the Roaming profile while every other Windows path says LocalAppData
findings.summary: `DefaultDirName={userappdata}\Programs\Trek` expands to AppData\Roaming\Programs\Trek. Install-Trek.ps1, Uninstall-Trek.ps1 and the release notes all use %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trek.
findings.failure_scenario: On a machine with a roaming profile, Trek's roughly 100 MB of binaries (plus Trek.old-<version> after each in-place update) are copied to and from the profile server at logon and logoff. The shipped Uninstall-Trek.ps1 defaults to the LocalAppData path, so run from the Roaming install it removes nothing there.
findings.evidence: installer.iss:16 `DefaultDirName={userappdata}\Programs\Trek`; Install-Trek.ps1:25 `Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\Trek"`; notes.sh:25 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Trek`
findings.suggested_fix: Use `{localappdata}\Programs\Trek` (or `{userpf}`).

findings.title: Working bar background-use chip overflows the thread pane when the right panel is open
findings.summary: The '<pointer> Search in the background  Show' chip does not shrink in a narrow thread pane. Its 'Show' button ends about 26 px past the composer card's right edge and the pointer sprite touches the label.
findings.failure_scenario: Open the Git panel (`trek-dev open tool:git`), turn the picture off in Settings > Tools & MCP, then `trek-dev open draft; trek-dev send --no-wait 'mock:background <window id> 800x600 Search'; trek-dev screenshot x`. The chip is cut off at the pane edge.
findings.evidence: /tmp/pipoff.png: the composer card ends at x~1267 (display px) and 'Show' ends at x~1293, with the pointer sprite at x~968-995 overlapping the start of 'Search in the background'. At full width the same chip lines up with the card edge.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the label truncate (min_w_0 plus ellipsis) so the chip fits the bar's width.

findings.title: Live page CSP is only a <meta> inserted after <head>, so page markup before <head> runs with no policy (the Mac also sends it as a response header)
findings.summary: `LivePage.document` puts the Content-Security-Policy in a `<meta http-equiv>` placed just after the first `<head…>` tag. The Mac serves the same document over its own scheme with the CSP as an HTTP response header as well (artifact.rs: "the CSP again — the response carries it too"). On the phone, an agent page that has a `<script>` (or any element) before `<head>` makes the HTML parser create an implicit head, ignore the later explicit `<head>`, and treat the injected meta as body content, where a CSP meta is ignored, so the page runs with no CSP at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A `trek-html` block of `<html><script src="http://attacker.example/x.js"></script><head><title>Hi</title></head><body>…` is run on the phone. tagEnd("head") finds the explicit `<head>`, so the CSP meta is inserted after it; the script before it has already executed and the meta lands outside the (implicit) head and is ignored. The page can then fetch/XHR over plain http and load http scripts/images, which the Mac's header-delivered policy forbids; `connect-src https:`, `img-src https:` etc. are void.
findings.evidence: ios/Trek/Views/LivePage.swift:158-168 `static func document(_ html: String, theme: LivePageTheme) -> String { let ours = "<meta charset…><meta http-equiv=\"Content-Security-Policy\" content=\"\(csp)\">… if let end = tagEnd("head", in: html) { return String(html[..<end]) + ours + String(html[end...]) } …`; :352 `web?.loadHTMLString(LivePage.document(html, theme: theme), baseURL: nil)` (no header path). crates/trek-core/src/artifact.rs:251-253 doc comment "the CSP again — the response carries it too"; crates/trek-app/src/artifact/native.rs:50-54 `.header("Content-Security-Policy", csp)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Serve the document through a WKURLSchemeHandler that sets the Content-Security-Policy response header (matching the Mac), or at least prepend `<!doctype html><html><head>…ours…` and strip/relocate any content that precedes the page's own <head>.

findings.title: A new snapshot never clears `unlisted`, so sub-agent/search rows removed while disconnected linger after reconnect
findings.summary: `handle(.snapshot)` replaces `threads`, `projects` and `agents` and merges `s.unlisted` in, but never drops entries of `unlisted` that the new snapshot no longer lists. Only a live `.threadRemoved` removes them. Rows that went away while the phone was disconnected (or during pairing with a previous Mac's data still in memory is reset, so only the disconnected case) stay in `unlisted` for the session.
findings.failure_scenario: Phone is in the background; on the Mac the user deletes a finished sub-agent thread (its parent remains). The phone reconnects: `welcome` + `snapshot` arrive; the snapshot's `unlisted` omits the deleted thread, but `unlisted[id]` still holds it. ThreadStatusStrip.earlier / AtWorkSheet list it under "Done" sub-agents and SearchView may show it; tapping it subscribes to a thread the Mac no longer has, producing an error toast and an empty transcript.
findings.evidence: ios/Trek/Model/AppModel.swift:305-313 `case .snapshot(let s): withAnimation { threads = s.threads; projects = s.projects; agents = s.agents; … } for t in s.unlisted { setUnlisted(t) }` (no removal); :329-331 `case .threadRemoved(let id): threads.removeAll {…}; unlisted[id] = nil` is the only place entries are removed outside reset(); ios/Trek/Model/AppModel+Reach.swift:22-24 `subAgentThreads(of:)` reads `unlisted.values`; ios/Trek/Views/Thread/ThreadStatus.swift:15-19 counts them as `earlier`.
findings.suggested_fix: In the snapshot case, rebuild `unlisted` from `s.unlisted` (keeping only ids present there or still referenced by an open store).

findings.title: reset() discards pending reply handlers without failing them, so awaiting continuations (attachments, note assets, background output, icon fetches) never resume
findings.summary: `failPending()` fails every awaiting request when the connection drops, but `reset()` (called from `attach` on re-pair and from `leave`) simply assigns `replies = [:]`. Requests built on `withCheckedContinuation` — `attachment`, `noteAsset`, `backgroundOutput`, and IconStore's `fetch` — are then suspended forever; the enclosing Tasks (and whatever they capture: the model, images) are never released, and the Swift runtime reports a leaked CheckedContinuation.
findings.failure_scenario: A thread with image thumbnails is open (several `attachment` requests in flight) and the user scans a new Mac's QR and confirms pairing. `pair()` → `attach()` → `reset()` clears `replies`. The Thumbnail `.task`s and any `BackgroundTaskView` polling loop stay suspended in `withCheckedContinuation` for the life of the process even though their views are gone; each leaked Task holds its captured `AppModel` closure and state. Same when the user taps Unpair.
findings.evidence: ios/Trek/Model/AppModel.swift:272-294 `private func reset() { … replies = [:] … }` (no callbacks invoked), versus :400-404 `failPending()` which calls each handler with an error; :221-227 `attach` calls `reset()`; :210-217 `leave()` calls `reset()`. ios/Trek/Model/Parity.swift:277-281, :293-297, :326-330 `await withCheckedContinuation { c in request(…) { reply in … c.resume(…) } }` resume only inside the reply closure; :409 IconStore fetch likewise.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `failPending()` (or equivalent) at the top of `reset()` so every outstanding continuation is resumed with an error before the map is cleared.

findings.title: "Fix with Agent" quotes lines from the file on disk, not the buffer the diagnostic refers to
findings.summary: Diagnostics come from the language server for the editor buffer, which may have unsaved edits. fix_problem builds the quoted snippet by re-reading the file from disk and slicing the diagnostic's line range out of that.
findings.failure_scenario: The user adds 20 lines at the top of main.rs without saving, and the server reports an error at line 45 of the buffer. 'Fix with Agent' quotes lines 42-48 of the saved file, which are different code. The chip says `main.rs:45` and the agent gets unrelated text. If the file is shorter than the line, `lines.get(a..=b)` returns None and the snippet is empty.
findings.evidence: panel.rs:118-122: `let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default(); let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect(); let (a, b) = (line.saturating_sub(PROBLEM_CONTEXT), (d.range.end.line + PROBLEM_CONTEXT).min(lines.len().saturating_sub(1) as u32)); let snippet = lines.get(a as usize..=b as usize)...`
findings.suggested_fix: Take the snippet from the open EditorView's text (EditorState value) when the file has a tab, and fall back to disk only when it does not.

findings.title: A failed autosave is only logged and the dirty flag is cleared, so the edit is silently abandoned
findings.summary: `flush` logs a `notes::save` error with tracing::warn and then sets `self.dirty = false` regardless. There is no toast and no retry. A later phone-triggered `reload` reads the old file and replaces the user's unsaved text.
findings.failure_scenario: The disk is full or the notes folder is read-only (sync conflict, permissions). The user types a long note and the 400 ms save fails. `dirty` is cleared, the UI looks normal, and nothing retries. The next `notes_epoch` bump calls `reload`, which re-reads the file from disk and overwrites the in-memory text, so the typing is gone. On quit, `flush` has nothing to do.
findings.evidence: notes.rs:368-378: `if let Some(note) = self.note() && let Err(e) = notes::save(note) { tracing::warn!("note {}: {e}", note.id); } self.dirty = false;`
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `dirty` true on error, retry on the next change or timer, and emit a Toast like the other note errors do.

findings.title: Sessions end while the thread waits for the user's approval, which also resets a tucked picture
findings.summary: `sweep` counts a thread as using the computer only while `run_state == Working` or it is waiting on sub-agents. `RunState::NeedsYou` (approval, question or plan review) is treated as the turn being over. After 5 seconds (LINGER) the session is dropped, and when it was the last one the picture closes and `tucked` is reset to false.
findings.failure_scenario: The user puts the picture away with X. The agent proposes its next click, and the MCP tool call needs approval, so the thread becomes NeedsYou. The user takes more than 5 seconds to approve. The sweep ends the session, finds none left, and sets `self.tucked = false`. After approval the click reports in, `record` runs, and the picture pops back open even though the user had put it away. Even without tucking, the picture closes and reopens during every slow approval.
findings.evidence: background_use.rs:274: `let working = ws.thread(&s.thread).is_some_and(|t| t.run_state == trek_core::RunState::Working || ws.waiting(&s.thread));`. background_use.rs:~283-288: `if empty { self.close(cx); self.tucked = false; self._watch = None; }`. types.rs defines `NeedsYou` as 'Waiting on an approval, a question or a plan review.'
findings.suggested_fix: Treat `NeedsYou` as still working in the sweep, ending a session only on Idle or Failed. Alternatively keep `tucked` until the user shows the picture again or a new turn starts.
findings.reason: ending the session on NeedsYou after 5 s is deliberate (documented in a comment); the narrow alternative is treating a pending tool approval as working

findings.title: Photos uploaded from phones are named by the second, so two uploads in one second overwrite each other
findings.summary: save_uploads names each saved photo `iPhone <YYYY-MM-DD at HH.MM.SS> <n>.<ext>`; the stamp has one-second resolution and the index restarts at 1 per request, so a second send (same phone double-tapping, a second phone, or a `new_thread` and a `send` within the same second) silently replaces the first message's image file while the first message still references that path.
findings.failure_scenario: Phone A sends a message with a photo to a working thread at 10:00:00 (queued; the agent reads the file when the turn starts). Phone B (or A again) sends a different photo at 10:00:00 to another thread. Both are written as `.../snapshots/iPhone 2026-10-15 at 10.00.00 1.jpg`; std::fs::write truncates and replaces. When the first thread's turn starts, the agent is given phone B's picture under phone A's message; the original is gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Include a unique component in the name (a counter or random suffix, or sub-second precision) and/or open with create_new so an existing name is never overwritten.

findings.title: `\text{` nesting recurses without a depth limit and can overflow the stack
findings.summary: `list` and `text_arg` are bounded by MAX_DEPTH (48), but `text_inner` calls itself for every `{` with no depth check. A closed formula of up to 20,000 characters (display math has no inline cap) can nest thousands of levels deep.
findings.failure_scenario: A model stuck in a repetition loop emits `$$\text{{{{…` thousands of braces and then `}$$`. Parsing aborts the process with a stack overflow, which cannot be caught. Reproduced with the real parse.rs: `\text{` plus 6000 `{` overflows a 2 MB stack in release ('has overflowed its stack ... aborting'); 19000 overflows too. The main thread has 8 MB, so it needs roughly 20k braces there.
findings.evidence: parse.rs:445-446: `'{' => { flush(&mut run, &mut out); out.extend(self.text_inner(face)); }` with no `self.depth` check, unlike `text_arg` (`if self.depth > MAX_DEPTH { self.rest_as_text() }`).
findings.suggested_fix: Increment `self.depth` in `text_inner` on `{` and fall back to `rest_as_text()` past MAX_DEPTH.

findings.title: A session of a stopped server rewrites devices.json from its stale registry, undoing a revoke or pairing made on the replacement server
findings.summary: After shutdown, each lingering session still runs `state.registry.touch(...)` when it finally closes, and DeviceRegistry::touch saves the whole device list from that (old) server's in-memory registry. Trek restarts the server in place (port/reach change, or automatically on any interface change via follow_addresses) and the new server loads devices.json immediately; a revoke or pairing done on the new server in the meantime is overwritten on disk by the old server's late save and comes back at the next load.
findings.failure_scenario: follow_addresses restarts the phone server (Mac wakes and rejoins Wi-Fi). A phone's old connection is dead, so the old session's close() spends up to 2 s draining (up to 12 s if the close frame write blocks) before reaching line 588. Meanwhile the new server starts (DeviceRegistry::load) and the user clicks Revoke on a device in Settings > Phone (registry.revoke -> save, file no longer lists it). The old session then runs touch(device_id) -> save() with its stale list that still contains the revoked device. The in-memory registry of the running server is correct, but on the next restart (the next network change) the revoked device is loaded back and its old token verifies again. Symmetrically, a device paired in that window is missing from the file and must pair again after the next restart. Because both servers live in one process, their saves also share the temp name `devices.tmp-<pid>` (pairing.rs:423), so two saves overlapping can leave a torn file that load() then moves aside as corrupt, unpairing every phone.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the post-session touch/save once shutdown has been requested (check `*inner.shutdown.borrow()`), or have shutdown() take the registry's path out so a stopped server never writes again; and give the temp file a unique suffix (counter or random) rather than the pid alone.

findings.title: Clicking a markdown link opens any existing local path with the system handler, including executables
findings.summary: The link handler resolves the URL with `link_path` (absolute, `~/`, `file://` or cwd-relative, only checked with `exists()`) and calls `cx.open_with_system(&path)` for anything that is not a showable image. That launches `.app`, `.command`, `.terminal` and similar on macOS, and `.exe`, `.bat` and `.lnk` on Windows. The path chips in the same file deliberately use `reveal_path` for files and open only directories.
findings.failure_scenario: A prompt-injected or careless answer includes `[Open the report](/tmp/report.command)` (or `file:///Users/me/Downloads/x.app`) after the agent wrote that file. The link looks like a document link. One click runs the script or app through LaunchServices, bypassing the shell-command approval the agent would otherwise need.
findings.evidence: md.rs:236-240: `} else if let Some(path) = link_path(url, link_cwd.as_deref()) { if crate::image_preview::showable(&path) { ... } else { cx.open_with_system(&path); } }`. Compare md.rs:422-427 where file chips use `cx.reveal_path(&path)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Reveal files (as the chips do), and open_with_system only directories or known document types. Alternatively ask first for executable types.
findings.reason: opening an existing local file with the system handler is documented behaviour; policy choice

findings.title: Any error reading settings.toml is treated as 'no file': Trek runs onboarding again and the next save overwrites the user's settings
findings.summary: load_checked maps every std::fs::read error (EACCES, EBUSY/sharing violation, EIO) to Settings::default() with no LoadProblem and no SaveGuard block, unlike a parse failure which blocks saves. Onboarding is then shown (completed=false) and finishing it, or any settings change, calls save(), whose rename-over replaces the still-intact file with defaults: projects, added agents, MCP servers, per-project prefs are lost.
findings.failure_scenario: settings.toml is temporarily unreadable at launch (e.g. owned by root with mode 600 after the data folder was touched by a sudo'd tool, or on Windows held with an exclusive lock by a backup/AV scanner at the moment Trek starts). read() fails → defaults, onboarding.completed=false, guard not blocked. The user clicks through onboarding → save() writes tmp and renames it over settings.toml (rename needs only write permission on the folder, which the user has) → the original settings are gone, with no .bad- backup since none is made on this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Only treat ErrorKind::NotFound as a missing file. For any other read error, return defaults with onboarding.completed=true, guard.block(...) and a LoadProblem{unreadable: true} so the toast explains and saves are refused until the file is readable.
